articleTitle: A modulation classification based on SVM
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we focused on the problem of automatic modulation classification of digital signals. Several useful characteristic parameters which can be used for modulation analysis are extracted from spectral correlation, for different types of modulated signals have different power spectral density functions. A density estimation approach based on Support Vector Machine (SVM) is developed. Also, a kind of Bayesian classifier is constructed using the estimated probability density. The experiment results demonstrated that the Bayesian classifier designed in this paper outperformed the traditional SVM classifier in the aspect of classification accuracy and training speed.

articleTitle: Crosstalk-aware provisioning strategy with Dedicated Path Protection for elastic multi-core fiber networks
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Space division multiplexing (SDM) over multi-core fiber (MCF) is advocated as a promising technology to overcome the capacity limit of the current single-core optical networks. Network survivability has become a more important concern to guarantee the QoS of more plentiful network traffics. In this paper, we have an investigation about dedicated path protection with considering inter-core crosstalk (XT) in elastic MCF networks. To minimize the influence of XT and blocking probability, a novel crosstalk-aware provisioning strategy with dedicated path protection (CaP) is proposed. Simulation results show that the proposed CAP strategy can perform better than the crosstalk unaware provisioning strategy (CuP), such as modified First-Fit (FF) strategy, in terms of blocking probability, and resource utilization.

articleTitle: IR/AR/MR service provisioning in elastic optical networks
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This work investigates the immediate reservation (IR), advance reservation (AR), malleable reservation (MR) service provisioning in elastic optical networks (EONs).We design request scheduling and/or routing and spectrum allocation (RSA) algorithms for the IR/AR/MR request, respectively. Simulation results show that the proposed IR/AR/MR service provisioning package can reduce request blocking probability effectively.

articleTitle: Multi-dimensional resource assignment in spatial division multiplexing enabled elastic optical networks with multi-core fibers
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, the problem of routing, core, and spectrum assignment (RCSA) for advance reservation (AR) and immediate reservation (IR) requests is studied in spatial division multiplexing enabled elastic optical networks (SDM-EONs) with multi-core fibers (MCFs). As lightpaths are set up and torn down, fragmentations may occur in both spectrum and time dimensions in SDM-EONs. To measure these fragmentations, we design a metric, named multi-dimensional resource compactness (MRC). Based on MRC, two RCSA algorithms are proposed, first-fit resource assignment algorithm based on MRC (FF-MRC) and random-fit resource assignment algorithm based on MRC (RF-MRC). Simulation results show that both FF-MRC and RF-MRC can achieve beer performance than the baseline algorithm in terms of blocking probability and spectrum utilization, with FF-MRC providing the best performance.

articleTitle: Failure recovery solutions using cognitive mechanisms for Software Defined Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Fault tolerance is one of the most desirable properties in optical networks. Meanwhile, the Software Defined Optical Network (SDON) is an innovative network paradigm that separates the control plane from the underlying data forwarding plane. Therefore, in this paper, we focus on the restoration mechanism for SDONs, and the out-of-band control is achieved for the communication between the controller and forwarding elements. Finally, we demonstrate the implementation of proposed resilience solutions mainly including failure detection scheme, dynamic routing algorithm and failure recovery application based on the SDON controller. Experimental results show the overall feasibility and efficiency of our method.

articleTitle: Fiber Bragg grating sensors for temperature monitoring in oil-immersed transformers
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A thermal sensor based on Fiber Bragg grating (FBG) is designed for online temperature measurement system in oil-immersed transformers. The measurable range is 30 °C to 150 °C, with resolution of 1 °C. Performance of the FBGs has been tested by temperature rising experiment in thermostat and online temperature measuring of transformer windings during short circuit experiment. Transformers equipped with the proposed FBG thermal sensors have worked stably for over a year, and the temperature data we achieved is stable and reasonable.

articleTitle: Data center networks recovery for large-scale disasters in optical cloud networks
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: With the growth of cloud computing and data center (DC), data center networks (DCNs) is becoming an increasingly important part in the future networks. However, large-scale disasters are considered as the main problems in terms of network survivability. Therefore, we propose a data center recovery algorithm to protect the majority of customer service as soon as possible. This algorithm can maximize time efficiency in maintaining network connectivity compared with traditional algorithm.

articleTitle: A Visible Light Communication based vehicle collision avoiding system
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Visible Light Communication (VLC) has many advantages including high bandwidth and low cost, which is widely accepted as one of the most promising technologies for future Intelligent Transport System (ITS). This paper presents a VLC based vehicle collision avoiding system focusing on most common seen rear-end collision scenario. Both theoretical analysis and numerical calculation are implemented to evaluate different configuration scenario. A demo system is designed and constructed to verify the scheme put forward.

articleTitle: A broadband compact 1×3 power splitter designed with inverse design method
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate a broadband 1×3 power splitter based on inverse design, with a compact footprint of 2.8 × 2.8μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and a power ratio of 25%:50%:25% at 1550nm. The insertion losses and ratio variations are less than 0.49dB and 4.4% in wavelength range from 1500nm to 1600nm, respectively. Further investigations show that the separated structure can be removed without degrading the performance of the splitter.

articleTitle: Power-over-fiber technique based sensing system for internet of things
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Internet Of Things (IOT) drives a significant demand in the extent and type of sensing technology and equipment. Sensors, control electronics and transmission units in such sensing systems will all need to be powered. How-ever, in a strong electromagnetic radiation area and other extreme environments, the electromagnetic inter-ference (EMI) is the key issue for power supply methods. A novel power supply method, which might overcome this issue, is the power-over-fiber (POF) technique. In this technique, the optical energy out of a high power laser is transmitted via a fiber and then converted into the elec-trical energy by a photovoltaic power converter (PPC) on the other fiber end. As a fiber is used instead of electric power cables, the delivery of the power is inherently immune to electromagnetic radiation. Recently, we have built up an optically powered active sensing system, supplying uninterrupted power for the remote active sensors and communication modules. Also, we have de-veloped a fiber-wireless sensor system based on the POF technique, to offer a flexible distributed sensing ability over a middle distance. In the demonstration system, a 2km away remote unit is optically powered and transmits back the sensing information, which is collected by a wireless sensor network (WSN) within a 50m range.

articleTitle: The PAPR reduction techniques based on WPT for CO-OFDM systems
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In coherent optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (CO-OFDM) systems, the high peak to average power ratio (PAPR) will causes serious signal degradation through the nonlinearity of modulator and fiber. In this paper, the PAPR reduction techniques based on wavelet packet transform (WPT) for CO-OFDM systems are proposed, the WPT is used instead of traditional fast Fourier transform (FFT). Moreover, two efficient PAPR reduction techniques are combined with the proposed WPT-OFDM. Simulation results show that the PAPR of proposed scheme combined with selective mapping (SLM) and partial transmit sequence in combination with clipping (clipping PTS) are optimized compared to the traditional FFT. Under the same conditions, while maintaining good performance in the BER compared to ordinary FFT. And the proposed WPT system provides the high spectral efficiency transmission without CP.

articleTitle: Design and test of geodesic dome phased array system for multi-target TT&C and communication
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: With rapid advance of space technologies, the number of on-orbit spacecraft will increase quickly in the future ten years, and then the traditional ground TT&C system based on parabolic antenna will not meet future requirements. Based on ideal spherical array antenna and Digital Beam Forming (DBF), a geodesic dome system for multi-target TT&C and communication is proposed and implemented. It can form multiple beams simultaneously in geodesic dome to track and communicate with multiple targets independently. Several demonstrations with satellite has performed and proved that the system realizes all designed functions and can meet our multiple-target TT&C requirements.

articleTitle: Tilted fiber Bragg gratings and its fiber humidity and twist sensing applications
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Recently, we had reported some fiber sensing applications by using the tilted fiber Bragg grating (TFBG), such as twist sensor, polarization sensor, curve sensor and relative humidity sensor, and so on. Here, we summarized two kinds of TFBG-based sensors (humidity- and twist-sensing) for the conference of ICOCN 2016. An optical fiber humidity sensors based on a graphene oxide coated on a TFBG and a fiber twist sensor based on the surface plasmon resonance (SPR) effect of an Au-coated TFBG were presented. The sensitivity of 0.129 dB/%RH with a linear correlation coefficient of 99% under the RH range of 10%~80% was obtained. For the twist ranging from 0 to 180° in clockwise or anti-clockwise directions, the proposed sensor shows sensitivities of 0.037 dBm/°(S-polarized), 0.039 dBm/°(P-polarized), respectively.

articleTitle: Development of optical fiber temperature sensor for aviation industry
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Temperature is an important monitoring parameter for applications in aviation industry. We have developed a series of optical fiber temperature sensors to fulfil the different requirements based on interference, including the pressure-based optical fiber temperature sensor with the capability of being integrated with optical fiber MEMS pressure sensor, micro-interferometer-based optical fiber medium temperature sensor with no special assembly process needed, and sapphire-solid-cavity-based high temperature sensor. The sensors all have compact structure and show good performance, which make them to possess a promising application prospect.

articleTitle: Static +dynamic bandwidth allocation for PON FC-AE-1553 network
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In order to meet the requirement of space payload system and the data transmission, a scheme of static and dynamic bandwidth allocation (SBA+DBA) of PON FC-AE-1553 network was proposed based on both theoretical analysis and simulation approaches. In our paper, the data type of payload was divided into periodic data, application data and burst data, the periodic data and burst data use the SBA and application data use the DBA scheme. The performances of the proposed scheme is evaluated and discussed, the best DBA cycle and node buffer should be set 4ms and 150 Mbit, and the maximum throughput of 32 nodes is 2.782Gbps.

articleTitle: FPGA-based 120Mbps online visible light communication system with RGB LEDs
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA)-Based online visible light communication system with RGB LEDs and ordinary PIN is implemented and demonstrated. The system uses simple OOK modulation. With the help of over-sampling technique at the receiver, the synchronization problem is solved. A bitrate of 120Mbps across 1m with the bit error rate less than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup> can be theoretically achieved without using clock and data recovery circuit(CDR).

articleTitle: Cross-layer design based ant colony optimization for routing and wavelength assignment in an optical satellite network
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A cross-layer based ant colony optimization (ACO) for routing and wavelength assignment (RWA) algorithm (CL-ACORWA) in an optical satellite network is proposed. The main objective is to enhance the network robustness. At first, a cross-layer optimization model is designed, which considers the Doppler wavelength shift of the physical layer and the transmission delay of the network layer. Then an ant colony optimization algorithm is utilized to search a path with the minimal transmission delay. Finally, the simulation result shows that CL-ACORWA has good performance in communication success probability. Compared with the minimum delay based ACO for RWA algorithm (MD-ACORWA), the communication success probability of CL-ACORWA can increase by 37% at most.

articleTitle: Real-time bi-directional visible light communication system
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A real-time bi-directional LED-to-LED VLC system is developed. The test results show that the proposed system can realize a downlink and uplink speed at 2.6Mbps and 2.55Mbps over a transmission range up to 2m.

articleTitle: Multi-broadband radio over fiber system based on Generalized Frequency Division Multiplexing
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We put forward and simulation demonstrated a multi-broadband radio over fiber (RoF) system based on Generalized Frequency Division Multiplexing (GFDM) by the using of Matlab software to call OptiSystem. The system simultaneously transmits four GFDM signals modulated to four different carriers. Each signal is with bit rate 10Gbit/s and bandwidth 2.5GHz and carriers are with frequency 10, 13, 16 and 19GHz respectively. The simulation results indicated that the signals can transmit through 24-km Single Mode Fiber (SMF) with EVM 2.6% when received optical power is −17.8dBm because of GFDM signals' ultra-low Out of Band (OOB) leakage to strictly avoid harmful interference to adjacent signals.

articleTitle: The period sensitivity and modal sensitivity of optical fiber force sensor based on mechanical induced ultra-long period fiber grating
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this study, a mechanical induced ultra-long period fiber grating (MULPFG) with periods of several millimeter is demonstrated. The periodic grooved plate used to create the grating in the single-mode fiber (SM600) is the rectangular grooved plate which is fabricated by the 3D printer. The experimental results clearly show that the MULPFGs with the longer grating period are more sensitive to the perturbation force than the shorter grating period. The force sensitivity to the resonance wavelengths of the MULPFG with higher modes are more sensitive than the lower modes. The fabricated force sensor based on MULPFG by using the 3D printer is robust and stable in operation and exhibits a high-sensitivity of ~ 0.470 nm/N. It offers the advantages of being inexpensive, erasable, and reconfigurable as well.

articleTitle: Fiber optic perimeter detection based on principal component analysis
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: It is a key requirement for any perimeter intrusion detection system to distinguish the intrusion from environmental events without reducing the efficiency. We implement and demonstrate a fiber optic perimeter detection system, which screens the event signal by its features in frequency domain. These features are extracted by method of principal component analysis (PCA) and then identified by support vector machine (SVM). Experimental results show that the combination of PCA and SVM improve evidently the anti-disturbance ability.

articleTitle: Inter-mode crosstalk compensation for radio orbital angular momentum multiplexing systems under misaligned condition using multiple-input multiple-output techniques
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Inter-mode crosstalk compensation in radio orbital angular momentum (OAM) multiplexing systems with misalignment between transmitters and receivers are investigated by utilizing the multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) analytical model. Both the zero-forcing (ZF) and minimum-mean-square-error (MMSE) compensation schemes are analysed under the misaligned conditions including off-axis and non-parallel cases. The simulation results show that system performance is significantly improved after compensation than that without compensation in both of the off-axis and non-parallel cases.

articleTitle: Low-complexity carrier phase estimation for M-ary QAM based on blind phase search using simplified measurement
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose and verify a carrier phase estimation algorithm for M-ary quadrature amplitude modulation (M-QAM) based on blind phase search (BPS). By replacing the complicated squared distance calculations with a simplified measurement in the real plane, the inherent computation complexity (CC) is reduced without performance degradation.

articleTitle: High-resolution radar imaging for non-sparse scatterers by the combination of non-convex regularization and total variation
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Most existing compressed sensing (CS) based radar imaging methods are based on the assumption that the targets are sparse enough, while in practice the targets are often spatially extended, which would degrade their inversion performances severely. In fact, the concentrations of the corresponding strong scatterers always form certain regions in high-resolution radar. Therefore, there still exist dependence and redundancy needed to exploit. In this paper, by utilizing the sparsity and continuity property of the targets, we propose a novel CS-based method for the radar imaging of two dimensional non-sparse scatterers, which is combining non-convex regularization and total variation constraint. Experimental results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Seamless all-optical bidirectional wavelength converter
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We proposed a seamless all-optical wavelength converter based on four wave mixing effect in highly nonlinear fibers. The proposed wavelength converter consists of a section of highly nonlinear fiber to implement bi-directionally wavelength conversion twice for seamless conversion. The seamless wavelength converter was utilized for orthogonal frequency division multiplexing signals with flexible spectra to defragment their optical spectra. The bidirectional scheme of the seamless wavelength converter costs less highly nonlinear fibers, so as to reduce the system size and cost.

articleTitle: Advanced fiber bragg grating for tunable microwave generation
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Frequency tunable microwave generation by heterodyning dual lasing lines from a fiber laser is presented. Different types of advanced fiber Bragg grating (FBG) based dual-passband filter are utilized in the laser cavity, including inverse-Gaussian apodized FBG, phase-shifted FBG, and phase-shifted chirped FBG.

articleTitle: Multimode fiber Fabry-Perot interferometer tip sensor
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate an optical Fabry-Perot interferometer fiber tip sensor based on an etched end of multimode fiber filled with ultraviolet adhesive. The fiber device is miniature and robust, in a convenient reflection mode of operation, has a high temperature sensitivity of 213 pm/°C within the range from 55 to 85°C, a good refractive index sensitivity of ∼−73.54 nm/RIU (refractive index unit) within the range from 1.332 to 1.372, and a high gas pressure sensitivity of −40.94nm/MPa. This device has a high potential in monitoring extreme environment of high temperature and pressure when Sapphire fiber and stable high temperature glue are employed.

articleTitle: Theoretical and experimental demonstration on narrow-linewidth DFB laser utilizing equivalent CPM-apodized grating
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Due to their various modulation formats, high receive sensitivity and spectral utilization efficiency, coherent optical communication systems are being invested to satisfy the future demands for huge traffic capacity. DFB lasers with narrow spectral linewidth are necessary for such systems, which limit the capacity of the whole system. In this paper, a low-cost narrow-linewidth DFB laser with equivalent CPM-apodized grating was demonstrated. The grating was fabricated by the reconstruction-equivalent-chirp (REC) technique based on conventional holograph exposure combined with lithograph technology. By employing the equivalent CPM-apodized grating, the spatial hole burning effect (SHB) in the DFB laser was significantly reduced. At room temperature, the linewidth of the laser is 224 kHz with injection current of 100 mA and side mode suppression ratio of 48 dB.

articleTitle: Photonic microwave multi-band frequency conversion scheme based on dual-OFCs for satellite communication
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A flexible and efficient frequency conversion method based on optical frequency comb (OFC) for satellite repeater applications is proposed. A dual-driven Mach-Zehnder modulator (DMZM) is driven by the received RF signal to perform SSB modulation. Two dual-parallel MZMs (DPMZMs) are used to generate two coherent OFCs. The key principle is to mix dual coherent OFCs that with different central frequencies. In the simulation, an input Ku band frequency of 15 GHz is successfully converted to 3 GHz, 7 GHz, 11GHz, 19 GHz, 23 GHz, 27 GHz, etc. in separate channels. The signal to noise ratio (SNR) of the multi-band LOs are between 28.83dB and 29.99dB.

articleTitle: Future of distributed fiber sensors (invited paper)
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Distributed fiber sensors offers an innovative technology for a spatially distributed measurement based on Raleigh, Brillouin and Raman scattering. By analyzing backscattered signal frequency, intensity and phase, one can realize a distributed measurement of strain, temperature and vibration over a tens of kilometers. This paper reviewed the history and current technology development of distributed time-domain fiber sensors in terms of spatial resolution and sensing range while present the standard operating principles. The future prospective view that can be extend further research development has also been discussed.

articleTitle: Sensing characteristics of CO2-laser written helical long-period fiber gratings
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrated the fabrication of the helical long-period grating (HLPG) in conventional single-mode fiber (SMF) by CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> laser. The surrounding refractive index and bending characteristics of the fabricated HLPG were investigated. Experiment shows that the fabricated grating has high refractive index sensitivity of -2321.67 nm/RIU. The resonance wavelength shifted to shorter wavelength linearly and the grating contrast decreased gradually as the curvature increased. The fabricated HLPG could have potential application on fiber sensors.

articleTitle: Multi-wavelength erbium-doped fiber laser based on four-wave mixing
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose and report on a novel multi-wavelength erbium-doped fiber laser (EDFL) on the basis of cascading of fiber Bragg gratings (FBGs) and four-wave mixing (FWM) effect in a highly nonlinear fiber (HNLF). A 1-km HNLF is incorporated in the laser cavity to eliminate the strong gain competitions in the homogeneously broadened erbium-doped fiber (EDF) by the degenerate FWM processes. Stable laser pulses at 1556.55, 1557.36, 1558.17, and 1558.98 nm are successfully obtained simultaneously and the spectrum is stabilized and the uniformity is less than 0.6dB.

articleTitle: An integrated single mode fiber communication and visible light communication system based on OFDM with Hadamard transform
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed an integrated single mode fiber (SMF) and visible light communication system based on Hadamard transform combined with orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM). The proposed scheme reduces the LED nonlinearity through reducing the high PAPR of the system. The results show that the BER of our proposed method has been improved.

articleTitle: Prediction for satellite communication based on data mining
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: To solve the problem of satellite communication down without preventive alarm, a predict method based on data mining is proposed. By quantitative analysis of history data the monitor records, the tendency of parameter which has a high relationship with the communication quality could be predicted. Thus, the ability of early warning for satellite communication is promoted efficiently.

articleTitle: A circular photonic crystal fiber supporting OAM mode transmission
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We proposed a new kind of circular shaped photonic crystal fiber, which can support large number of good quality orbital angular momentum (OAM) modes, with good features of large separation of effective indices, low confinement loss, flat chromatic dispersion and small nonlinear coefficient, over wide bandwidth. With all these good features, the proposed circular photonic crystal fiber could be a good promising OAM fiber for mode division multiplexing in high capacity fiber communication systems.

articleTitle: UWB signal generation based on XGM effect in a DFB laser
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel scheme to generate ultra-wideband (UWB) signals based on cross-gain modulation (XGM) effect in a DFB laser is proposed. In this scheme, a gain-switched laser (GSL) is used as master laser (ML), the optical pulses are optically injected into a DFB laser, which is used as slave laser (SL). By proper system configuration, UWB monocycle, doublet or triplet UWB signals can be generated after detection by a balanced photodiode. Besides, other modulation formats can also be realized, such as on-off keying (OOK) and pulse amplitude modulation (PAM) by properly modulating the ML optical pulses. Finally, fiber transmission of the modulated UWB signals is experimentally investigated.

articleTitle: Subpixel edge detection of inner hole for ceramic optical fiber ferrules
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Concentricity is the most important parameter to show the quality of the ceramic optical fiber ferrules. The diameter of its inner hole is micron. Therefore, the method of image detection is suitable to detect the edge of the inner hole. In this paper, we firstly introduce some common subpixel detection algorithms. Then three different kinds of edge gray models are presented. Finally, according to the gray scale characteristics of edges of inner holes, we put forward a subpixel edge detection algorithm by using the gradient fitting method based on the Gauss function. Besides, polynomial interpolation method and gray moment method are also used to detect the edge of the image. The experimental results show that: the gradient fitting method based on the Gauss function has the higher precision than other methods.

articleTitle: Research of on-board optical burst switching weight-weighted round robin assembly algorithm based on the QoS guarantee
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of on-board optical burst switching assembly algorithm cannot realize completely QoS guarantee, an on-board optical burst switching weight-weighted round robin assembly algorithm based on the QoS guarantee(QWRRA) is proposed in this paper. In this assembly algorithm, IP packet will be inserted in different queue according to the different destination and QoS level when arrive at edge node LEO, the assemble scheduler removes the IP packet from the queue according to the weight-weighted round robin mechanism and assembles the IP packet. When the assemble scheduler generates a burst data packet, it will detect the length of each queue, and change the weights of the queue. Simulation studies the transmission delay and throughput performance of the algorithm, then compared with the assembly algorithm based on mixed threshold and round-robin scheme(FZTFR) and assembly algorithm based on maximum length and maximum time(MSMAP). The results show that the proposed algorithm improves the transmission quality of high priority IP packet and guarantees the transmission of lower level IP packet at the same time.

articleTitle: A higher power and high efficiency supercontinuum generated by small core UHNA3 fiber
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Generation of super-continuum by using 5 m ultra-high NA silica optical fiber (UHNA3) with core diameter 1.8 μm and mode-field diameter (MFD) ~2.6μm is compared with Photonic Crystal Fiber (PCF). A 1064 nm gained switched pico-second semiconductor pulsed laser source is used to study the performance of supercontinuum generation and the amplified signal is coupled by direct splicing with UHNA3 fiber or PCF. Analysis of spectral evolution of the supercontinuum generated under various conditions is performed. Higher output power and lower splice loss is observed in UHNA3.

articleTitle: Magnetic field sensor based on concatenation of fiber peanut and long-period fiber grating with resolved temperature cross sensitivity
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A compact dual-parameter sensor based on a fiber-optic interferometer consisting of a peanut fiber taper and a long-period fiber grating integrated with magnetic fluids has been proposed and experimentally demonstrated. By employing a sensor matrix containing distinct magnetic field intensity and temperature sensitivities of different interference dips, simultaneous dual-parameter measurement could be achieved.

articleTitle: Outage performance analysis of all-optical amplify-and-forward relaying over dual-hop optical inter-satellite link
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, outage performance of dual-hop optical inter-satellite link (OISL) employing all-optical amplify-and-forward (AOAF) relaying is analyzed. Take into account the combined source-to-relay (S-R) and relay-to-destination (R-D) channel attenuation induced by geometric spread and pointing error within outer space environment, a series of closed-form expressions for outage performance are derived. Numerical results indicate that the performance of AOAF relaying dual-hop systems is low-complexity and has better performance than that of the non-relay systems under the same total power consumption.

articleTitle: Minimized power consumption in survivable virtual optical networks mapping
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper develops a minimum-power mapping algorithm (MPMA) to minimize power consumption and introduces a random-node mapping algorithm (RNMA) for comparison. Simulation results show that MPMA not only minimize power consumption, but also reduce spectrum resources compared to RNMA.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of radio over intersatellite optical wireless communication system
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a complete modelling and analysis of radio over IsOWC system with an optical booster amplifier and an optical preamplifier is presented. The influence of satellite vibration and bias voltage of the electrooptical modulator is analysed. The closed-form expressions for average RF gain and noise figure are derived. Numerical results for RF gain and noise figure are given for demonstration. Results indicate that the gain of optical preamplifier can obviously improve the performance of the proposed system and the optimal bias voltage exists.

articleTitle: Femtosecond laser micromachining of microfluidic fiber sensors
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Migration of lab-on-chip configurations into the optical fiber platform opens the revolutionary prospect of lab-in-fiber systems on the basis of an efficient optical transport highway for multifunctional sensing. In this paper, three-dimensional microfluidic channels patterning inside the fiber by femtosecond laser ablation, femtosecond laser assisted splicing and selective chemical etching will be introduced in terms of machining mechanism and accuracy. In these approaches, we have successfully achieved phase-shifted FBG sensor based on in-grating bubble and several in-fiber cavity based interferometric sensors and also preliminarily explore their applications in biochemical analysis.

articleTitle: Self-oscillating triangular pulses generator based on an optoelectronic oscillator
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this letter, a self-oscillating triangular waveform generator based on an optoelectronic oscillator (OEO) was demonstrated. As a result, 5.35 GHz full-duty-cycle triangular pulse trains were generated via a phase modulator cascaded with a Mach-Zehnder interferometer. Microwave signals were also generated with phase noise of -124dBc/Hz at 10 kHz offset.

articleTitle: Broadband microwave measurement based on photonics technologies
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Microwave measurement refers to the acquisition of parameters of a microwave signal or the identification of properties of an object using microwave-based approaches. Thanks to the broad bandwidth and high speed provided by modern photonics, microwave measurement in the optical domain can provide better performance in terms of bandwidth and speed which may not be achievable using state-of-the-art electronics. In this paper, techniques for photonics-based broadband and high-speed microwave measurement are discussed with an emphasis on the measurement of parameters of a microwave signal and the identification of properties of an object.

articleTitle: Simulation of the optical generation monocycle and doublet UWB signals based on the polarization modulation
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A method to generate a monocycle UWB and doublet based on polarization modulation is proposed. Two Gaussian pulses with opposite polarity are phase-modulated to the orthogonal optical carriers with the polarization modulator (PolM). Then an appropriate group delay is introduced by polarization maintaining fiber (PMF), and a monocycle UWB is generated. The polarity of the generated monocycle UWB can be controlled via changing the angle between the signal polarization direction and PMF principal axis by polarization controller (PC). Two monocycles UWB with opposite polarity combine and generate doublet UWB when an appropriate time delay is introduced. Monocycle and doublet UWB with a central frequency of about 5.36GHz and 5.83GHz, a 10dB bandwidth of about 8.96GHz and 7.36GHz, and a fractional bandwidth of about 167% and 126 % are generated. They both meet the FCC standards.

articleTitle: Bidirectional mobile fronthaul based on wavelength reused MDM
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a cost effective wavelength reused mode-division-multiplexing (MDM) system for high speed symmetrical bidirectional mobile fronthaul application. At the base band unit (BBU) pool, one of the spatial modes is used to transmit signal carrier while the others are used for downstream signal channels. At the remote radio unit (RRU) side, the signal carrier is firstly mode demultiplexed and then selected to be reused as modulation carrier for all the upstream signal channels. Thanks to the low mode crosstalk characteristic of the mode multiplexer/demultiplexer (MUX/DEMUX) and few-mode fiber (FMF), the signal carrier and each signal channel can be effectively separated. The spectral efficiency (SE) is significantly enhanced when multiple spatial channels are used. With the proposed scheme, we demonstrate a proof of concept intensity modulated 4×25-Gb/s 16-QAM orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) transmission over 10-km FMF using low modal-crosstalk two-mode FMF and MUX/DEMUX with error free operation.

articleTitle: Wavelet transform filtering method of optical fiber Raman temperature sensor
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The traditional wavelet filtering threshold de-noising method is widely used in the optical fiber Raman sensor temperature measurement, but the weakly spontaneous Raman scattering signal is easily submerged by optical noise and random noise. So the method has a low efficiency. In order to increase the efficiency of signal denoising in the process of temperature measurement, we proposed a new method combine default threshold and the given threshold based on the traditional method. The experimental data of 25Km fiber Raman sensor is filtered by the new method and the results show that the new threshold method can eliminate the noise in the signal, and also preserve the information of temperature variations.

Author Keywords: Distributed optical fiber Raman temperature sensor

articleTitle: A novel multi-controller flow schedule scheme for Fat-tree architecture
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: OpenFlow is currently the most commonly deployed Software Defined Network (SDN) technology. Some deployments designed with multi-controller OpenFlow have better scalability than standard OpenFlow. However, these deployments are not optimized for the Data Center Network (DCN), the cross-controller communication and routing may be inefficient. In this paper, we present the communication mechanism design and implementation of optimized multi-controller OpenFlow for the Fat-tree through three aspects: partition scheme, routing algorithm and cross-controller communication. The result shows that our design performs well in terms of bandwidth and latency.

articleTitle: Measurement of phase retardation in a liquid crystal variable wave retarder using a polarizing triangular interferometer
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The purpose of this study aims to investigate a new method for measuring the phase retardation caused by the induced birefringence from a liquid crystal sample. The method uses a polarizing triangular interferometer whose arrangement requires just a few optical devices. The liquid crystal phase retarder under investigation is inserted into an optical path of the triangular interferometer. The modified interference beam, therefore, is used to characterize the sample property. The method is proved to be effective and suitable for the measurements of polarization related parameters of the optical devices.

articleTitle: Routing and spectrum assignment algorithm with prediction for elastic optical networks under self-similar traffic
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Poisson traffic model was usually used in existing investigations for evaluating the performance of routing and spectrum assignment (RSA) algorithms in elastic optical networks (EONs). However, many studies showed that the self-similar traffic could reflect the Internet traffic property more accurately than Poisson traffic. In addition, the performance of RSA could be improved by using the predicted holding time awareness in EONS. In this paper, we propose a dynamic RSA algorithm that achieves better performance by using Back Propagation neural network (BPNN) to predict the information of each future connection with holding time awareness under self-similar traffic. Experimental results show that the proposed RSA algorithm could obtain lower blocking probability compared to existing RSA algorithm under self-similar traffic.

articleTitle: Hybrid EDF/Brillouin laser for discriminative measurement of strain and temperature
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Discriminative measurement of temperature and strain sensing is proposed and experimentally demonstrated based on erbium-doped fiber laser (EDFL) and Brillouin erbium fiber laser (BEFL). The EDFL and the BEFL share the same laser cavity. The EDFL can be easily switched to BEFL when the Brillouin pump is injected into the cavity. Longitudinal modes beat frequency generated from EDFL and Brillouin frequency shift originated from BEFL are monitored to discriminate strain and temperature. The simultaneous measurement errors of strain and temperature are within ± 25.8µε and ± 0.8°C.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of pilot-based OFDM channel estimation for hybrid PLC&VLC system
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Visible light communication (VLC) has been a research hotspot for broad bandwidth, high speed, and anti-interference. Power line communication (PLC) has the advantages of low cost and flexible access, which is connected and combined with VLC to be a hybrid communication system. We set up a communication system model of PLC&VLC based on orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) modulation, and investigated four pilot-based channel estimation methods. Least squares (LS) and singular value decomposition (SVD) criterion are both insensitive to block-type pilot space. By contrast, we found that discrete fourier transform (DFT)-based technique can improve the performance of LS combined with linear interpolation, and the performance of SVD combined with linear interpolation is similar to that of SVD combined with DFT-based interpolation. Considering the performance and complexity of algorithms, SVD combined with linear interpolation is the best choice of the four methods.

articleTitle: Modeling and analysis for watchful sleep mode in PON power management
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In watchful sleep mode for PON, the power consumption and average transition delay are the most important and conflicting performance index, and influenced by the sleep state duration. In this paper, we have modelled for watchful sleep mode based on Markov chain to analyze system performances. Through the numerical analysis, we can find that the ESE can be improved to ≥ 70% and the average TD is no more than 35ms, when the sleep state cycles (n) are 20.

articleTitle: Implementation and experimental demonstration of a real-time 7-DSSS VLC system based on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a real-time seven-direct-sequence spread-spectrum (7-DSSS) visible light communications (VLC) system based on field-programmable-gate-array (FPGA) is implemented and experimentally demonstrated. We add interference light in our field experiments to build the multipath environment. And then, we measure the bit error rate performance of both on and off keying (OOK) and 7-DSSS VLC systems for different bit rates over a transmission distance of 1.5 m. The results show that using the DSSS technique in VLC system the multipath induced interference is suppressed thus leading to improved performance.

articleTitle: All-optical high-speed temporal random pattern generation based on photonic time stretch
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a novel all-optical temporal random pattern generation scheme based on photonic time stretch involving cascaded Mach-Zehnder interferometers (MZIs) with different chirped spectral response. The overall spectral response represents a broadband random spectral pattern. Temporal random patterns can then be generated thanks to photonic time stretch which mirrors spectrum encoding to temporal waveform. Tuning of the generated temporal patterns is achieved using a rapidly tunable optical delay module in one of the MZIs.

articleTitle: Fault tolerant bit number optimization of channel coding based on probability statistics method
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An optimization method is proposed which can effectively reduce the impact of the difference between effective data bit error rate and telemetry frame synchronization code error rate when channel coding is used in space telemetry tracking and command (TT & C) system. Firstly, theoretical analysis of frame synchronization theory, error rate calculating methods and fault tolerant bit number optimization principles are given in detail. Then, experimental results are obtained including the optimal bit number with (1/3, turbo) channel coding and 1M bit rate. Both theoretical and experimental results indicate the method proposed here is effectively which has potential applying value for fault tolerant bit number selecting during channel coding in TT & C system.

articleTitle: A decision feedback channel estimation approach of the satellite mobile communication system
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper we present a decision feedback channel estimation way for the mobile satellite communication system in order to improve the bit error performance. The transmission is disturbed not only by shadowing and multipath effects and additive white Gaussian noise, but also by the weather attenuation. The conventional Least Square(LS) is not well suited to detect the transmitter sequence, whereas the LS-based decision feedback is able to take into account the fading channel and therefore is able to detect the signal much better. The LS-based decision feedback channel algorithm first estimate channel response, then the estimation channel response use decision feedback estimation to get the next frame channel response. Our simulation results show that LS-based decision feedback channel estimation algorithm performs much better than the origin LS channel estimation method in terms of bit error rate(BER) with a gain of probably 1 dB.

articleTitle: An anomaly traffic detection method based on the flow template for the controlled network
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The current network anomaly traffic detection technologies usually focus on the rules matching and statistical method which are suitable for the general network environment. For the communication characteristics of the controlled network environment, this paper puts forward a network anomaly traffic detection method based on the flow template, which captures and analyses the real-time network traffic. The method aims to detect the anomaly network traffic by extracting the characteristics of the network traffic and behaviour, establishing the flow template based on the network eight-group information, and comparing the established template with the actual traffic. The final experiment results show that the method can accurately detect the anomaly network traffic in the controlled network environment.

articleTitle: Polarization beam splitter based on lithium niobate thin film
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A polarization beam splitter based on lithium niobate thin film is proposed, which consists of a directional coupler. The device is easy to be achieved by simple structure. Numerical simulations show that the device has a good performance for the separation of TE and TM polarizations with a high extinction ratio (about 30 dB). The simulated fabrication tolerance for the variation of the waveguide width is about 110 nm and the bandwidth is about 70 nm for the extinction ratio higher than 10 dB.

articleTitle: Shared protection algorithm based on virtual network embedding framework in Fiber-wireless access network
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: To achieve the Fiber-wireless (FiWi) access network's seamless networking as well as to alleviate bandwidth tension, network virtualization is applied in FiWi networks. With the virtualization of the network, the growing number of people share the same physical resources. However, network components, once out of order, will inevitably bring a lot of loss to more users. Meanwhile, if a node or link fails, there may be several VNs affected. Taking the importance of the protection of FiWi access network with virtualization into account, we propose shared protection mechanism which is embedded for improved Dijkstra routing algorithm to the network in order to improve its security. Through the simulation results, we can see that the shared protection mechanism of can improve the success rate of data transmission of FiWi access network by taking up some of the network resources.

articleTitle: Simultaneous temperature and refractive index measurement based on optical fiber sensor
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An optical fiber senor based on Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) is proposed and experimentally demonstrated for the measurement of temperature and refractive index(RI) simultaneously. This structure is composed of a pair of spherical-shape structures and an embedded taper, where the spherical-shape structure excites high-order cladding modes and the taper enhances the penetration depth of evanescent field. Experimental results show that the interference peaks of the transmission spectrum have different sensitivity to temperature and RI, so that a matrix can be used to achieve the simultaneous measurement of the temperature and RI. Within the range of 10-100°C and 1.3432-1.4026RIU, temperature and RI resolution of ~0.22°C and 1*10^-4RIU have been achieved by intensity-modulation. We also find the temperature resolution is 0.37°C by wavelength-modulation. The structure is compact, low cost, and applied to various fields to achieve simultaneous measurement of temperature and RI.

articleTitle: A modified Viterbi and Viterbi phase estimation scheme in faster than Nyquist optical communication system
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Faster than Nyquist optical communication system recently attracts more and more attentions because of its higher spectral efficiency than ordinary Nyquist systems. In this work, we propose a modified-Viterbi and Viterbi phase estimation (VVPE) carrier phase recovery (CPR) scheme which shows an effective capability of reducing the cycle slips induced by inter-symbol interference (ISI) in a fast-than-Nyquist (FTN) optical coherent communications system. In a 28-Gbaud FTN polarization-division multiplexed (PDM)-QPSK optical communication system, the comparison of the proposed modified-VVPE scheme and the conventional VVPE scheme is carried out. It is proved that the proposed modified-VVPE scheme can effectively overcome error carrier phase estimation, which leads to a better BER performance.

articleTitle: OFDM and self-coherent detection based satellite-to-ground communication system
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a scheme using Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) and self-coherent detection to enhance satellite-to-ground data links, with improved communication data rate and detection performance. We analyzed this free space optical communication systems theoretically, with preliminary experimental results being demonstrated. In the experiment, quadrature phase shift keying and 16-quadrature amplitude modulation OFDM signals were transmitted and detected by coherent receiver respectively.

articleTitle: LED-induced fluorescence spectroscopy technique for milk freshness detection
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A LED-induced fluorescence spectroscopy system is developed to detect milk freshness. In this paper, milk samples stored at room temperature are excited by a LED at 380nm and their fluorescence spectra are detected by a compact spectrometer. The detection is processed at intervals of several hours. The principle component regression(PCR) method is used to establish a predictive model of milk freshness. This system can also be applied to other similar food detections.

articleTitle: Analysis and simulation on error propagation in inertial horizontal coordinate system of space tracking ship
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Data errors of shipborne radar in inertial horizontal coordinate system are influenced by several aspects, such as measuring errors of equipment, ship-swaying and hull deformation(collectively called ship attitude). In this paper, based on the process of tracking ship's data managing, error propagation model of ship attitude errors and equipment's measuring errors from telemetering coordinate system to inertial horizontal coordinate system is built up. Numerical simulation results indicate that ship's position errors can not be ignored, and the influence between distance measure and angle measure is not very strong. The relationship between azimuth error and elevation error are rather complicated, and the influence of elevation error on azimuth error is stronger than that of azimuth error on elevation error.

articleTitle: Graphene-assisted multiple-input high-base optical computing
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We fabricate a nonlinear optical device based on a fiber pigtail cross-section coated with a single-layer graphene grown by chemical vapor deposition (CVD) method. We demonstrate 10-Gbaud three-input quaternary hybrid addition and subtraction (A+B−C, A+C−B, B+C−A) in the experiment.

articleTitle: Spectrally overlaid DDO-OFDM transmission enabled by optical power division multiplexing
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Two 8.3-Gb/s spectrally overlaid DDO-OFDM signals are successfully transmitted along 50-km SMF using optical power division multiplexing and received by a successive interference cancellation (SIC) receiver. Spectral efficiency is doubled with optimized optical modulation index and optical power division ratio.

articleTitle: Study of strain-compensated for 1310nm AlGaInAs/InP multi-quantum-well laser
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This article reported on strain-compensated quantum well structure for AlGaInAs/InP and used the ALDS to do numerical simulation for lasers. It can be concluded that the introduction of appropriate strain opposite to well layer strain in barrier layer can improve the energy band structure of quantum wells and the limitation carriers. After testing, the laser had a low threshold current of 13.4mA and a slope efficiency of 0.54W/A at 25□. The quality of the quantum well has been improved by optimizing its strain and adopting strain-compensated methods.

articleTitle: Low power consumptions voltage control oscillator uses PMOS elements optical sensor application
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This letter proposes a UMC CMOS low power consumptions voltage control oscillator fabricated in the 0.18 µm UMC CMOS process and describes the circuit design, operation principle and measurement results of the low power consumptions voltage control oscillator. The low power consumptions voltage control oscillator circuit is composed of a LC dual-resonance. The low power consumptions voltage control oscillator uses PMOS transistor to degrade the power consumptions and phase noise. At the supply voltage of −0.9V, the dc power consumption is 1.78mW. This low power consumption oscillator tuning range is from 1.92GHz to 1.98GHz for optical sensor application.

articleTitle: User access of space communication networks: Challenges and system analysis
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: As an important infrastructure, space information network is based on platforms such as satellite, balloon and airplanes, it acquires, transfers and processes real-time information and can support ocean going, emergent rescue, navigation and spacecraft tracking, deep space exploration and dynamic, high-rate data transmission. When ground users access the space information network, the channel will be more complicated than those of ordinary space communication or terrestrial wireless communication. In this paper, a system model of ground user accessing the space networks is described. Technical challenges are analyzed and possible approaches are proposed.

articleTitle: Low power VCO using Gm-Boosting technique for optical pulse trains application
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This letter presents a 0.7V low power Voltage Control Oscillator (VCO) is designed and implemented in a 0.18µm COMS 1P6M process. This circuit is using Gm-Boosting technique that can reduce power consumption. At the supply voltage 0.7V, the output frequency is 2.228GHz and the phase noise is −121.56 dBc/Hz at 1MHz offset. Tuning range is about 113MHz(4.9%) between 2.228 to 2.341GHz while control voltage was tuned from 0 to 2V. Excluding output buffers the VCO consumes the power 0.7 mW under a standard supply of 0.7 V for optical pulse trains application.

articleTitle: MOSA: A modular all-optical switching architecture for data center networks
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The massive adoption of cloud-based services in data center lead to an exponential increasing in both the amount traffic and servers, which brings a great challenge to data center network (DCN). In this paper, MOSA: a modular all-optical switching architecture based on arrayed waveguide gratings (AWG) is proposed to address the issue. The modular design makes MOSA can expand up to millions of servers easily. Because of the all-optical design, MOSA can carry a great mount traffic. The simulation results demonstrate that although the scale of MOSA becomes larger, the network latency is almost remaining the same, besides, MOSA will not saturate even at a very high traffic load.

articleTitle: Refractometer based on SMS interferometer with two waist-enlarged tapers
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A compact refractometer by using interferometer in SMS structure with two waist-enlarged tapers is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. It is fabricated by splicing a short section of multimode fiber (MMF) between two single-mode fibers with two bitapers. A refractive index sensitivity of 152.2nm/RIU with a measurement range of 1.3725–1.462 is achieved. The temperature effect of the proposed refractometer is also discussed.

articleTitle: High-resolution angle measurement based on the statistical method
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Azimuth radar echo can be seen as the convolution of antenna pattern and target backscatter coefficient. Traditional methods of radar angle measurement use the deconvolution techniques with poor anti-noise performance. This paper firstly analyzes the causes of single channel deconvolution morbid. Then, based on the signal modeling and analysis process, a high-resolution angle measurement algorithm which combines the signal statistical model is proposed by taking the azimuth angle measurement as solving linear equations. The proposed method, which includes the targets' prior distribution information, is an improved signal modeling. Compared with the existing reconstruction approaches, it can achieve more robust inversion. Simulation results show the feasibility of the proposed method, especially its adaptability under low SNR.

articleTitle: 2.03–2.80 µm supercontinuum generation in an all-fiberized holmium-doped ZBLAN fiber amplifier
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A supercontinuum spanning from 2.03 to 2.80 μm was generated in an all-fiberized holmium-doped ZBLAN fiber amplifier. Low-loss and robust fusion splicing was achieved between silica fiber and holmium-doped ZBLAN fiber. A 2050-nm Q-switched fiber laser with pulse of 20 kHz, ~20 ns was used as the seed laser. The amplifier was in-band pumped by a homemade continuous-wave fiber laser operating at 1950 nm. A supercontinuum with power of 147 mW and spectrum spanning from 2.03 to 2.80 μm was obtained. This work is the first demonstration, to the best of authors' knowledge, of a supercontinuum source based on an all-fiberized ZBLAN fiber amplifier.

articleTitle: Switchable absorber by vanadium dioxide
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper we numerically simulate a broadband absorber made of Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> and phase transition material vanadium dioxide (VO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>). Its structure consists of three layers: VO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> grating array, Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> film, and VO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> film at the bottom. As temperature increasing from 30°C to 85°C, VO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> varies from the insulator to metal phase. Simulation result shows that there is four times enhancement of absorption by temperature increment. And when it is 85°C, this GIM structure absorbs light span from 1000 nm to 2000 nm. At 2000 nm, it shows nearly perfect absorption. This switchable broadband absorber has great application potential in sensors and testing technology.

articleTitle: High-frequency Pound-Drever-Hall sensing of a short and high-finesse fiber ring resonator
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A resonant micro optic gyro (RMOG) equipped with a short and high-finesse fiber ring resonator employing the high-frequency Pound-Drever-Hall (PDH) modulation is proposed and demonstrated. The modulation frequency and index of the PDH modulation are optimized to maximize the slope of demodulation curve. Based on the optimum parameters, the lock-in accuracy of the resonant frequency servo loop in the RMOG is improved to 0.178°/h, which is almost improved by two orders of magnitude compared with that obtained for the low-frequency phase modulation.

articleTitle: Hollow core Bragg fibers for miniaturization of fluorescence sensors
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Hollow core Bragg fibers (HC-BFs) with a conventional multilayered cladding or with a defect layer are employed to realize a miniaturized and highly sensitive fluorescence sensor. The performance of our proposed fluorescence sensor strongly depends on the large core HC-BF that simultaneously acts as a sample cell, a fluorescence collector and a filter for the noisy excitation light. Notably, both the photonic bandgap effect and the transverse resonant behavior can be used for filtering the noisy excitation light mixed in the fluorescence. Finally, two presented examples verify the validity and feasibility of the design principle.

articleTitle: Temperature-compensated AC current sensor using tandem flat-topped fiber Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An intensity-demodulated AC current sensor system, which compensated the background temperature, was proposed and demonstrated. Temperature-compensated current detection is achieved by designing a novel sensor head which makes a pair of flat-topped FBGs (FT-FBGs) having differential current responses and the same temperature responses. As a result, optical intensity after the two tandem FT-FBGs varies monotonously with measured current and has no relation to the background temperature. The experimental results shows that the minimum ac current of 2.4 A is detected by the sensor and a linear relationship in the range of 0-426.0 A is obtained.

articleTitle: A new multicast aware optical Network-on-Chip
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A multicast aware optical Network-on-Chip is proposed in this paper. The new architecture employs broadband microring resonators to reduce the number of microring resonator and decrease the complexity of the system. According to the evaluation analysis, the proposed architecture could reduce the number of MRs by 62.5%, the insertion loss by 34.5% and the power consumption by 11.2% at most.

articleTitle: BBU aggregation for maximizing the resource utilization in Optical-Enabled cloud radio access networks
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Optical-Enabled cloud radio access network (CRAN) divides legacy base station into remote radio heads (RRH) and centralized baseband units (BBU) pools. In this paper, we focus on the improvement of BBU resource utilization, and propose a BBU aggregation by dynamically awaking and sleeping BBU cards under time-geometry pattern. We discuss the BBU capacity model, and two heuristic algorithms are developed to minimize the number of active BBU cards. Simulation comparisons are performed between two kind of different cell sites. Numerical evaluations show that BBU aggregation can significantly increase the BBU utilization.

articleTitle: Multimedia multicasting oriented resource allocation of C-RAN with optical fronthaul
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Cloud radio access network (C-RAN) opens up new opportunities to have a better resource management of mobile network on the basis of centralized processing. The fronthaul, which transfers signals between baseband units (BBUs) and remote radio units (RRUs), is confronted with bandwidth allocation problem when multimedia multicast technique is introduced. In this paper, we propose an algorithm using integer non-linear programming (INLP) model to improve the bandwidth allocation efficiency of fronthaul considering of information sharing in multicast. Good results can be achieved in the numerical simulations.

articleTitle: A photonic cystal fiber sensor based on spherical-shape structure cascaded with core-offset structure
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A photonic crystal fiber (PCF) sensor based on spherical-shape structure cascaded with core-offset structure is proposed and fabricated. The sensor head is composed of PCF and spherical-shape structure cascaded with core-offset structure which are made by the single mode fiber. The temperature and refractive index(RI) are measured by the sensor. Experimental results show temperature sensitivity and refractive index sensitivity are 8.13pm/°C and 188.09nm/RIU, respectively. It can be widely applied in biological and medical sensing.

articleTitle: Phase-OTDR based on space difference of Rayleigh backscattering
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Phase-OTDR based on space difference of Rayleigh backscattering is proposed. The Rayleigh backscattering from different segments of the test fiber interfere by adjusting the path difference of the imbalance Michelson interferometer. According to the resemble polarization and intensity of two path light, amplitude, frequency of the acoustic signal at the different locations along the sensing fiber can be simultaneously demodulated, and we realize the acoustic signal demodulation of different intensities..

articleTitle: Multi-octave mid-infrared supercontinuum generation in dispersion-engineered AlGaAs-based strip waveguides
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose and numerically investigate mid-infrared supercontinuum generation in dispersion-engineered Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.18</sub>Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.82</sub>As-based strip waveguides. An ultra-board supercontinuum ranging from 2 to 15.9 μm is obtained when pump pulses with center wavelength of 4.1 μm and peak power of 3.35 kW are used.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of IP network traffic monitoring system
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Network packet capture and analysis technology is a cornerstone of network security and protocol analysis technology. On the analysis of the LAN IP network traffic monitoring requirements, this paper detailed introduces the design ideas of traffic monitoring system based on WinPcap technology, expounds the key technologies and features in the process of system implementation, focusing on huge amounts of packet processing technology, task dependent protocol data analysis technology, and behavior decision technology based on the strategy. Tests show that the system can realize IP data flow quickly and accurately capturing and business analysis, and determining whether the business is legally and effective according to the network administrator predefined behavior strategy, and gives tips with intuitive and friendly information. The system meets the actual needs.

articleTitle: Thermal control system design of the demodulator for fiber optic sensors
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The fiber optic sensors have been widely used in the aircraft industry for the structural testing and health monitoring. The demodulator is an important part of optical fiber sensing system, and it is sensitive to the extreme temperatures which are very common in aerospace field. In this paper, a new design for the thermal control system of demodulators is presented based on the study of the inner structure and the heat source distribution of the demodulation system. The design extends the working temperature range of the demodulator to -40°C to 70°C by the proper use of natural cooling method and accurate heating control system. Compared with the traditional design, the demodulator is smaller in size and has less energy consuming. The environment tests in different temperatures are performed and the results validate the efficiency of the design.

articleTitle: Design for shared backup path protection based on content connectivity against disaster in elastic optical datacenter networks
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Disaster, natural or man-made, is the main threaten of survivability and reliability of networks. The development of content connectivity provides a new way of protection against disaster to ensure the reliability of network service/content. This paper focuses on shared backup path protection based on content connectivity against disaster in the context of elastic optical datacenter networks. In this work, we propose an integrated Integer Linear Program (ILP) for an optical datacenter network design to minimize both the required spare capacity and the working resources. We also propose a heuristic algorithm for large datacenter networks.

articleTitle: Non-local means denoising based on noise level estimation for BOTDA
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A noise level estimation algorithm based on selected weak patches is utilized to ensure the non-local means denoising performance for Brillouin optical time domain analyzer (BOTDA). We firstly study the accuracy of proposed method by simulation. Then, we use non-local means to process the experimental data with different estimation method, proving the reliability of proposed approach.

articleTitle: An optimized RWA method with services selection based on ACO in optical network
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Focusing on the RWA problem in optical transmission network, we proposed an optimization algorithm with a requests selection rule based on Ant Colony Algorithm framework. The way of choosing a request from demand space was introduced, which would improve algorithm optimization ability. This method could reduce network traffic congestion effectively. At last, we simulated it on a province electric power communication network.

articleTitle: Prediction-based and provident service degradation in optical data center networks
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we describe a prediction-based and provident service degradation algorithm for optical data center networks. We allocate the computing and network resources by considering the results of the prediction model and the provident service degradation jointly. The simulation results show that the theoretical prediction well matches the actual network traffic, and the average absolute value of the relative error is less than 10%. On the other hand, our proposed algorithm can increase the provider profit and reduce network congestion.

articleTitle: Reflective index sensors based on tilted fiber Bragg grating inscribed in the thin-core fiber
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A compact optical fiber reflective index sensor is proposed and experimentally demonstrated.
