It is based on the tilted fiber Bragg grating (TFBG) inscribed in the thin-core fiber that is downstream spliced to the conventional single mode fiber (SMF). Thanks to the core dismatch between the SMF and the thin-core fiber, more cladding modes can be recoupled back into the SMF .The sensor can be used to detect the change of surroundings refractive index (SRI). Besides, the sensor can solve the problem of cross-sensitivity between SRI and temperature.

articleTitle: Numerical investigation on atmosphere refractivity distribution and turbulence's influence on earth-satellite laser communication
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Theoretical model is built up to investigate earth-satellite laser communication numerically, where atmosphere affects the communication effect greatly. The distribution of atmosphere refractivity and turbulence are two main aspects in atmosphere's influence on earth-satellite laser links. Simulation based on angular spectrum theory is performed to study laser propagation through atmosphere to outer space, and different distribution of atmosphere refractivity is discussed. Then the astronomical refraction errors introduced by atmosphere refractivity are investigated. At last, the influence of turbulence on laser patterns and propagation angles are discussed.

articleTitle: 2.5Gbit/s MDM transmission over 180m two-mode fiber using 1550nm SFP without MIMO processing
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: 2.5Gbit/s MDM transmission over 180m two mode fiber is experimentally demonstrated using compact SFP modules without MIMO processing. Compared to single-mode launch conditions, the OSNR requirements for dual-mode transmission is increased by 9dB.

articleTitle: Supercontinuum generation with a repetition rate over 100MHz based on a picosecond pulse from a normal dispersion fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An all-fiber supercontinuum (SC) source with a repetition rate of over 100 MHz is experimentally demonstrated for the first time. The SC is generated by introducing the pulse output from a normal dispersion fiber laser into high nonlinearity fibers (HNLFs). An erbium-doped fiber amplifier (EDFA) and single segment single mode fiber (SMF) are used to compress the pulsewidth to increase pulse peak power. Finally, we can successfully obtain a SC with 10 dB bandwidth of over 500nm. In particular, the spectrum at the C-band is flat with a power fluctuation of less than 3 dB. All those features verify the SC an excellent local oscillator source for linear optical sampling application.

articleTitle: OAM generation in optical fibre and free space devices
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Orbital angular momentum (OAM) beam generation has been investigated using all-fibre and free space configurations. In the first approach, the composite fused coupler is based on a single mode fibre (SMF) and an air-core fibre. The second approach exploits geometrical phase introduced by nanostructuring of silica glass. Both approaches are demonstrated to achieve power coupling efficiencies in excess of 80% at telecom wavelengths.

articleTitle: Discussion on space-earth integration transmission mechanism of space information network based on CCSDS protocols
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: To suit the change of the current space transmission network from the single bus network to the complex multistage switching network, a data exchange mechanism is proposed based on CCSDS protocols including uplink data transmission format and downlink data transmission format. It can solve the problem that the single level network can not be solved the uplink data distribution at the two kinds of states, as well as multi-level backup and independent scheduling for the downlink data, thus saving channel resources and isolating fault.

articleTitle: Grouped LR-EPON with WDM-OFDM-TDM DBA algorithm and sleep-based energy-efficient mechanism
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose an energy-efficient mechanism and a corresponding multi-dimension dynamic bandwidth allocation (DBA) algorithm for long-reach Ethernet passive optical networks (LR-EPONs). Time delay was reduced and upstream bandwidth was increased by 10%, and energy saving is increased by 90% when load is small.

articleTitle: Method of ship-rocking forecasting based on statistical physics
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The ship-rocking is a crucial factor which affects the accuracy of the ocean-based aerospace vehicle measurement. Here we have analysed groups of ship-rocking time series in horizontal and vertical directions utilizing a Hilbert based method from statistical physics. Based on these results we could predict certain amount of future values of the ship-rocking time series based on the current and the previous values. Our predictions are as accurate as the conventional methods from stochastic processes and provide a much wider prediction time range.

articleTitle: Comparison of swarm intelligence methods for suppressing PAPR in CO-OFDM systems
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Swarm intelligence algorithms are applied to suppressing peak to average power ratio (PAPR) in CO-OFDM system by optimizing phase of subcarriers. The result shows that all of these algorithms can effectively reduce PAPR, and the PAPR of CSO optimized signal is reduced by 1.5dB, 0.77dB and 0.28dB compared with that of PSO, BSA and BA optimized signals.

articleTitle: Research on timing synchronization algorithms for CO-OFDM systems
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A timing synchronization algorithm with a new timing metric function is proposed for CO-OFDM system. Simulation results show that the MSE of the proposed algorithm is very close to zero in the system without chromatic dispersion, even though the OSNR is low. And it can provide higher accuracy comparing with other methods when the dispersion reaches 18ps/nm/km.

articleTitle: Robust multi-rate hierarchical coded modulation based on Star-QAM and hybrid coding correction
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper presented a multi-rate Star-QAM encoding and decoding method based on the hierarchical coding which could be adjusted to achieve the channel coding efficiency and modulation. The design is based on the combination of soft / hard decision in layered decoding. We have successfully increased BER performance to 0.5dB which achieved 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> when SNR is 11 compared to no stratification codec considering the iteration is 5 in the process of coding.

articleTitle: Efficient location proof with location tags in database-driven Cognitive Radio Networks
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Database-driven CRN is vulnerable to spoofing attacks. In this paper, we identified proactive location spoofing and passive location cheating attacks in database-driven CRN. Consequently, we proposed a novel and efficient location proof scheme via location tags collected from the LTE paging channel. Then, we adopted private equality test technology to test whether two location sketches matches, which generated by user and his proofer that we called “Referee”, using shingling technology. With the proposed scheme, the user can prove his location without revealing his accurate information to the database. Our experimental results showed that our approach could provide location proof effectively.

articleTitle: Enhanced performance of in-band OSNR monitor based on delay time optimization of interferometer
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose and experimentally demonstrate a method of choosing optical delay time by calculating normalized autocorrelation function of channel noise to achieve optimal OSNR monitoring performance. Up to 29 dB monitoring range with error ≤±0.5 dB for 112 Gbit/s PM-QPSK signal is obtained. We also demonstrate the method is applicable to the filters with different bandwidths and different shapes.

articleTitle: Ytterbium doped LMA-W-DCF for high power fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose and demonstrate the Large-Mode-Area-W-Type Double Clad Fiber (LMA-W-DCF) for high power fiber laser system. The proposed fiber structure is capable of filtering the higher order modes of the system. Using the in-house fabricated fiber, we achieved output power of about 630 W with optical to optical slope efficiency of about 68 % and M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x,y</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 1.42 and 1.38 respectively.

articleTitle: Adaptive HPA Back-Off algorithm for interactive mobile satellite broadcasting system
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of introducing additional Total Degradation (TD) in adaptive satellite system caused by fixed High Power Amplifier (HPA) operating point, the paper proposes an adaptive HPA Input Back-Off (IBO) algorithm carried out on the gateway side in the Forward Link of the system based on Adaptive Coding and Modulation (ACM) techniques. On the other hand, the traditional way of evaluation of system-level TD would cause inaccurate assessment if used in adaptive forward link satellite system, so Dynamic Real-Time Total Degradation (DRTTD) is proposed to evaluate overall system performance. Results show that, with the adaptive HPA IBO algorithm adopted, the whole system can obtain system-level DRTTD performance better. This indicates that more appropriate integral HPA's operating point can be obtained in the adaptive forward link of the interactive mobile satellite broadcasting system with the proposed adaptive HPA IBO algorithm than traditional fixed HPA's working status situation.

articleTitle: Experimental study on slow light based on all-optical wavelength conversion and dispersion medium
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Slow light delay based on all-optical wavelength conversion using four-wave mixing (FWM) and dispersion medium is experimentally studied. Firstly, all-optical wavelength conversion with band-width of 28.4nm (from 1549.3nm to 1520.9nm) by FWM in 1500m dispersion flattened highly nonlinear fiber (DF-HNLF) is realized. Then, the maximum delay of 12.0ns is experimentally achieved by transmitting the original signal and wavelength-converted signal in 3.88 km dispersion compensating fiber (DCF). The experimental results are in good agreement with the principles.

articleTitle: Passively Q-switched erbium-doped fiber laser with graphite saturable absorber based on the pencil-sketching at 1.56 µm region
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate a passively Q-switched erbium-doped fiber laser with graphite saturable absorber (SA) produced by a pencil-sketching method. Using our SA, it is shown that Q-switched pulses can be obtained from erbium-doped-fiber ring cavity. The Q-switched pulses of a 1.98 µs pulse width are readily obtained at a repetition rate of 46.08 kHz.

articleTitle: Comprehensive assessment of optical network in power grid
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an evaluation method to assess the optical network in the power grid. A set of evaluation indices is selected to characterize the different aspects of the network. Not only the network reliability but also the service support ability and the network developability are taken into consideration, which leads to a comprehensive evaluation result. The assessment is based on a hierarchical model and an evaluation algorithm. An example is presented to show the detailed operation of the evaluation process and verify the effectiveness of the given approach.

articleTitle: Multi-dimensional resource defragmentation (MDRD) based on cluster SDON controller (CSC) paradigm in spatial division multiplexing enabled elastic optical networks (SDM-EON)
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Cluster software defined optical networking controller (CSC) paradigm is exploited for multi-dimensional resource defragmentation (MDRD) in spatial division multiplexing enabled elastic optical networks. Experimental results show that spectral and spatial resources can be reorganized fast and effectively with cluster control technology.

articleTitle: Curvature sensor based on an LPG written in an air-clad thin-core fiber
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we report a curvature sensor based on an LPG written in an air-clad thin-core fiber (AC-TCF). The achieved curvature sensitivity is -0.226 nm/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> with a good linearity with R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> value of 0.991. Unlike conventional LPGs, this AC-TCF LPG is insensitive to the variation of surrounding refractive index, due to the existence of the one ring of large air-holes in the cross section of the AC-TCF.

articleTitle: Research on the reliability of IP network based on NQA
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: More and more attention is paid on the reliability of IP network as it becomes the current main business network. Especially for real-time communication, link fault may cause severe result. Thus, quick switch between master and slaver link is need. Using Network Quality Analyzer (NQA) technology, the network performance (such as response time, network jitter, packet loss rate and so on) can be detected in real time. On this basis, with the statistics of the real-time network performance data and linkage function, it is an effective way to realize quick link switch and improve the reliability of IP network.

articleTitle: SDNyquist platform for big data transmission
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: To realize high-speed big data transmission, we combine the advantages of Nyquist Super-channel and Software Defined Optical Networks (SDON), thus establishing the SDNyquist platform that dynamically manages the whole optical network. This platform has the features of flexible resource allocation, high spectrum efficiency and global network optimization with the help of Routing, Modulation Level and Spectrum Allocation (RMLSA) algorithm. We compare the performance of different SDNyquist platforms based on RMLSA and traditional RSA. Experimental results show that our SDNyquist platform based on RMLSA has high potential in improving network performance.

articleTitle: Applications of chaotic laser in optical communications
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Laser chaos has wide applications in field of optical communication. Besides optical chaos communication, laser chaos can be used in random bit generation, lidar and optical time-domain reflectometer. This paper reviews our recent results of chaos-based optical time-domain reflectometer and random number generation in our group. In addition, we present that chaotic laser can be utilized to generate white noise with a 3-dB bandwidth of 14GHz.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of a fast tunable laser based on DFB semiconductor laser array using reconstruction-equivalent-chirp (REC) technique
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a novel approach of fast tunable laser, which uses high-speed driving circuit and DFB semiconductor laser array to achieve the fast switching of wavelength. We use single chip microcomputer and FPGA to form the control system, and a high-speed driving circuit to ensure the switching speed. The 8-channel DFB laser array was fabricated based on reconstruction-equivalent-chirp (REC) technique. The experimental result shows that the switching time of the wavelength is about 30 ns.

articleTitle: A compact on-chip triplexer based on Bragg grating-assisted multimode interference couplers
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A silicon triplexer based on Bragg grating-assisted multimode interference (MMI) couplers is demonstrated. Compared with the conventional MMI based triplexers, the device length is not required to be the common multiple of beat length of the self-imagings. The fabricated device shows extinction ratio (ER) higher than 15 dB and insertion loss (IL) around 1 dB in all output ports.

articleTitle: A temporal cloak based on ultra-short-pulse generation and time-domain fraunhofer diffraction
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Recent research has revealed a significant ability to manipulate and control a light beam to hide events in time-domain. Achieving highly functional temporal cloaking, which open up and subsequently close intensity gaps in the probe beam to conceal events from the observer with satisfied performances, are still difficult in optical fiber communication. Here, we propose and experimentally demonstrate a temporal cloak system based on ultra-short-pulse generation and time-domain fraunhofer diffraction. We succeed in hiding 83 percent of the whole time axis and cloak pseudorandom dark return-to-zero data bitrate at 10 Gbit/s. The four states of temporal cloaking and condition of cloaking off have been investigated in this paper.

articleTitle: The design of millimeter-wave quasi-optical power synthesizer
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The high power technology is widely applied in satellite communication and military systems. Based on the theory of beam waveguide(BWG) as well as polarization wire grid,we presents a quasi-optical power synthesizer working at millimeterwave band. The designed power synthesizer can make electromagnetic wave traveling in two different ways with orthogonal polarization directions and combine them at a common output port. The designed quasi-optical synthesizer is fabricated and tested. The tested transmission efficiency of the two ways is above 83% and the designed synthesizer can working with a peak power of hundreds kilowattt(KW).

articleTitle: 2 µm mode-locked fiber laser with a carbon nanotube absorber
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate a 2 μm passive mode-locked fiber laser. A single-wall carbon nanotube (SWCNT) is used as saturable absorber. Thulium-doped fiber (TDF) is used as the gain medium. The output wavelength is grating stabilized to 1998.85 nm by a high reflective (HR) fiber Bragg grating (FBG) together with a two by two coupler. A 8.22 MHz fundamental mode-locked pulsed laser with output signal power of 4.68 dBm is produced.

articleTitle: Design and fabrication of multi-wavelength 1.3µm AlGaInAs/InP distributed feedback laser array for radio-over-fiber system
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Design and fabrication of multi-wavelength 1.3µm AlGaInAs/InP distributed feedback (DFB) laser array for analogy radio-over-fiber (RoF) system is proposed. The performance of the DFB laser such as high power, low noise, wide modulation bandwidth, high linearity has to be improved to meet the increase demand of the analogy RoF system. Here, we designed the structure of the MQWs to increase internal quantum efficiency and decrease the noise, optimized the parameter of the DFB grating to obtain high SMSR, and utilized BCB RWG to broaden 3dB bandwidth. A 4-channel multi-wavelength DFB laser array proposed was fabricated. Single longitude mode (SLM) operation was obtained with SMSR>46dB for all the lasers. The experimental results of the spectra have good agreement with simulation results. The typical slope efficiency was 0.445mW/mA. And the typical OCS and CTB of the laser diode are −66.3dB and −68.1dB, respectively. The 3dB bandwidth of the directly modulation can reach 15GHz. The linearity is high. The proposed multi-wavelength DFB laser array can be a promise candidate component for RoF system for multi-band and multi-service.

articleTitle: A method of target fusion detection based on the multi-fractal analysis
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A target detection method is proposed which is based on the multi-fractal spectrum characteristics of the remote sensing image. The method uses multi-fractal spectrum to reflect the image global features and effectively suppress noise characteristics at the same time. The membership function is constructed by multi-fractal spectrum of visible and SAR images to indicate the uncertainty of their sensors information. The trade-off between the intersection operation and union operation of the feature level fusion detection is achieved by the membership function, in order to reduce the false alarm rate and the missed alarm rate. The experimental results show that the method can combine the respective advantages of SAR and visible images, and effectively improve the accuracy of detection.

articleTitle: Improved laser-induced deposition of silver nanoparticles on fiber end for surface-enhanced Raman scattering
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper demonstrates an improved laser-induced deposition of silver nanoparticles method based on fiber surface micro-grating for surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS). The femtosecond (fs) laser ablation is used to create a roughened surface with micro-grating structures on the cleaved fiber end, which is beneficial for silver nanoparticles growth, and then the end of the fiber probe is immersed in a reaction solution for deposition of silver nanoparticles with a 785 nm exciting laser beam coupled into the fiber probe. The experiment results show that a larger number of silver nanoparticles have deposited on the roughed end using laser-induced method compared with the flat fiber end under the same induction conditions, leading to a better performance for the R6G molecules detection (about 32 times). Our rapid prepared fiber SERS probe provides a feasible method for real-time, high performance and remote measurement of the SERS signal in biochemical analysis.

articleTitle: All-fiber laser wavelength measurement system based on two quadrature Faraday rotation devices
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The laser wavelength measurement and tracing in real time is very important in the optical fiber sensing field. The current wavelength measurement methods are mainly based on the interference technique, such as Michelson wavemeters, which are expensive, heavy and slow. In this manuscript, we reported a all-fiber, totally passive, wavelength measurement system base on Faraday rotation devices. This laser wavelength measurement method is composed of specially designed fiber magneto-optic devices and balanced detectors. When the linearly polarized lights with different wavelengths pass through the magneto-optic crystal, their polarization planes will be rotated at different angles, then the light wavelength can be measured by detecting the rotated angles. We also discussed the accuracy improvement solution based on quadrature detection technique.

articleTitle: Influence of coatings on bending sensing properties of long period fiber gratings
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Two different long-period fiber gratings (LPFGs) are inscribed by high frequency CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> pulse laser. Coatings effects on inscribed LPFGs bend sensing characteristics are researched. The experimental results show that coatings effects on bending strain characteristics of LPFGs are more obvious, and LPFGs with coatings have more higher strain sensitivity, it is more suitable for used in bending sensor measurements.

articleTitle: The beat-length of polarization-maintaining few-mode-fiber measurement based on polarized interference
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Polarization-maintaining few-mode fiber (PM-FMF) is a new kind of fiber that is envisioned to have applications in optical communications and sensors. But characterization methods for PM-FMF have not been established. In this paper, the method of beat-length measurement based on polarized interference is extended to the PM-FMF and the beat-length calculation formula of PM-FMF is deduced for the first time. Mode coupling, which exists in PM-FMF is not present in single-mode polarization-maintaining fiber (PMF), can be effectively differentiated by Fourier transform of the modulated spectrum. The measurement system is quite simple and easy to be implemented. The beat-length of each mode can be tested.

articleTitle: A novel multi-LDPC-NPPM modulation coding scheme for satellite ground laser communications
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An efficient modulation and coding scheme combined with multiple LDPC codes and PPM modulation is proposed to mitigate the effect of atmospheric turbulence, which can have an unfavorable impact on the reliability of the communication link in the laser channel of the integration network of satellite and ground. The research is mainly about the reliability of the communication link under different orders and parameters of the PPM modulation. The result shows that it can effectively enhance the link reliability if the system uses the scheme of 8PPM and 1/2 code rate binary LDPC coding under different turbulent intensity. Comparing and analyzing the scheme of binary and multiple LPDC coding system, we found that the scheme combined with the multiple LDPC codes and PPM modulation and coding is more efficient than binary LDPC codes related programs.

articleTitle: Recent advances in slow polarization dynamics of ultrashort laser pulses
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: By using a carbon nanotube based ultrafast fiber laser system, we have investigated the polarization dynamics of ultrashort laser pulses in the soliton regime. Various types of polarization trajectories have been found on the surface of Poincare sphere. Alternative strange attractors embedding on a two dimensional surface has been identified. We have reviewed the recent advances and development in polarization dynamics via using fiber based ultrafast lasers.

articleTitle: Shared risk link groups-aware virtual link mapping in packet optical transport networks with multi-mode fibers
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Mode-spectrum matrix is introduced to describe the multi-dimensional resources in packet optical transport networks (POTN) with multi-mode fibers (MMF), based on which a novel shared backup path protection algorithm is proposed to optimize the allocation of optical resource during virtual link mapping (VLM) in packet optical transport networks.

articleTitle: In-line mode equalizer with large equalization range by femtosecond-laser-light refractive-index modifying
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An in-line mode equalizer for LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode and LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode which is useful for mode-division-multiplexing system is proposed and characterized numerically in this paper. The design is based on microstructuring the refractive-index profile of a two-mode fiber with femtosecond-laser-light iradiation technique. Compared with current equalization methods, this scheme has the advantage of large equalization range and low loss.

articleTitle: Amplified spontaneous emission noise in few-mode fiber Raman amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We present a theoretical model of amplified spontaneous emission noise in few-mode fiber Raman amplifiers. Under the undepleted-pump approximation, equalization of modal gain also ensures equalization of OSNR. This modal allows the prediction of mode-dependent OSNRs in the saturated-pump regime. The experimental results are in good agreement with theoretical estimations.

articleTitle: Initial appearance and maximum conversion of modulation instability in optical fiber
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Based on the numerical simulations of the generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLSE), initial appearance and maximum conversion of modulation instability (MI) are investigated on different noise conditions in optical fiber. Furthermore, considering the noise condition, the expressions of critical power for MI threshold and maximum power conversion are obtained.

articleTitle: An exact VNE algorithm based on Integer Linear Programming
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: One main challenge in network virtualization is known as virtual network embedding(VNE). VNE is NP-hard and most algorithms in the literature are heuristic. This paper presents an exact algorithm based on the Integer Linear Programming(ILP). The exact algorithm aims to simultaneously minimize the cost of substrate network and average virtual link delay of mapped VNRs. Simulation results reveal that the exact solution VNE-ILP outperforms the state of art heuristics in terms of VNR acceptance ratio and average virtual link delay.

articleTitle: Photonic generation of power-efficient UWB pulses adaptable to multiple modulation formats using a dual-drive Mach-Zehnder modulator
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A simple scheme to generate power-efficient FCC-compliant UWB pulses is proposed by using a dual-drive Mach-Zehnder modulator (DD-MZM). By adjusting the working parameters of the DD-MZM, a UWB quasi-quadruplet pulse with a spectral power efficiency of 49.2% and a 10-dB bandwidth of 6.22 GHz is obtained via computer simulations. Furthermore, this UWB generator can potentially support multiple modulation formats, including pulse polarity modulation, pulse-position modulation, on-off keying, and pulse-amplitude modulation. Since a single laser source is utilized, the proposed system is tolerant to fiber dispersion, and compatible with existing WDM-PONs.

articleTitle: Photonics devices fabricated using ultrafast laser direct-write techniques
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The design and challenge for fabricating photonics devices in bulk glass using ultrafast laser direct-write technique were presented. With a focus on monolithic designing, the design of complicated photonics devices starts with a waveguide structure, followed by several structures that can be used for different functions.

articleTitle: A novel magnetic fluid based all-fiber-optic vector magnetometer
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate a compact all-fiber-optic vector magnetometer based on Mach-Zehnder interferometer by utilizing magnetic fluid filled double-clad photonic crystal fiber (DC-PCF). The magnetic fluid (MF) serving as crucial sensing elements is injected into the micro-channel-arrays of DC-PCF. The magnetometer is constructed by splicing a section of MF-filled DC-PCF between two standard single mode fibers forming a high stable all-fiber structure without any additional sealed capillary. The vector magnetometer has the capability of simultaneous measurement of magnetic field intensity and orientation by monitoring a specific dip wavelength shift or transmission loss of Mach-Zehnder interference spectrum. The magnetometer with response sensitivities of 114.5 pm/mT, 1.79 dB/mT (X-axis) and 41.9 pm/mT, 0.52 dB/mT (Y-axis) at two orthogonal magnetic field orientations was fabricated and investigated.

articleTitle: Nonlinear noise in 400G optical fiber communication systems
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The influences of nonlinear propagation effects on three typical 400 Gb optical fiber communication systems with different modulation formats, including dual-carrier 16-quadrature amplitude modulation (Dual-16QAM), single-carrier 16QAM (Single-16QAM) and four-carrier quadrature phase shift keying (Four-QPSK) are investigated by numerical simulations. System performances are compared for those 400G systems, as well as standard 100 Gb/s/ch system. Both single channel and multichannel cases are considered.

articleTitle: Design of mixed HCG/DBR multilayer reflectors
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We design a kind of mixed high-index-contrast subwavelength grating/distributed Bragg reflector (HCG/DBR) multilayer reflectors. The mixed HCG/DBR multilayer reflectors provide a broadband high reflectivity characteristic with several pairs which can replace conventional DBRs of InP-based materials. By applying the epitaxial lateral overgrowth (ELO), the design structure turns into a virtual InP substrate for growing InGaAsP/InP active regions without wafer bonding and it can be applied to some optical devices such as vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers (VCSELs) and resonant cavity enhanced (RCE) photodetectors. Here some structure parameters (pairs, period and duty cycle) are optimized to achieve broadband high reflectivity by numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Sensitivity characteristics of LPFGs inscribed in FMF
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Few mode fiber (FMF) has been studied a lot in recent years. It is told that the co-propagating coupling between different modes in few mode long-period fiber gratings (FM-LPFGs) can get a large sensitivity in sensing measurement. In this paper, we present a comprehensive simulation about the sensing sensitivity of long-period fiber gratings (LPFGs) inscribed in few mode fiber (FMF). We recognize a sensitivity factor which contributes a lot to the sensing sensitivity, and calculate the value in FMF. Our analysis reveals a high sensitivity factor at the resonance wavelength of 1550nm when the resonant cladding mode order equals to 20. Our simulation proves that LPFGs inscribed in FMF, comparing with sing mode fiber (SMF), have a much better sensing performance in the temperature, strain and surrounding refractive index (RI) when the cladding mode order is closed to 20. Particularly, the maximum value of RI sensitivity can reach 1512 nm/10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup> in FMF when the surrounding RI equals to 1.43, five times as much as the value in SMF.

articleTitle: An effective RSA scheme under the consideration of diffserv QoS in multi-domain heterogeneous software defined optical network
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, for the purpose of supporting an end-to-end business process with guaranteeing the quality of transmission (QoT) of signal in multi-domain heterogeneous software defined optical networks, we emphatically design routing and spectrum assignment (RSA) algorithm to establish optical paths and allocate spectrum resources. The simulation results verified that compared with distributed scheme, the proposed algorithm can reduce overall network blocking probability.

articleTitle: Intensity-resolved high sensitivity transverse load sensor based on an in-line M-Z interferometer
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A simple and low cost transverse load fiber sensor based on in-line Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) is proposed. The sensor head is formed by a single mode fiber-polarization maintaining fiber-single mode fiber (SMF-PMF-SMF) structure through core-offset fusion splicing. With the increasing of transverse load on the PMF, the couple efficiency between the core mode and the cladding mode of PMF decreased, which further brings about a change of the interference fringe visibility. The experimental results show that the structure with a 1.3 cm-long PMF has the sensitivities of 12.85 dB/(N/mm) and 30.69 dB/(N/mm) for the fast and slow axes resonant wavelengths of 1517.1 nm and 1551.3 nm, respectively, which are about 2 times higher than that of the current similar existing transverse load sensor.

articleTitle: An optical fiber humidity sensor based on Mach-Zehnder interferometer coated with a composite film of graphene oxide and polyvinyl alcohol
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An optical fiber humidity sensor based on Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) was proposed. The MZI consists of two waist-enlarged tapers and a single mode fiber (SMF). The SMF between the two tapers was coated with a composite film of graphene oxide (GO) and polyvinyl alcohol (PVA). The finite element software called COMSOL Multiphysics was used to analyse the energy distribution in the sensor. The sensor was put inside a little chamber and a hygrometer was used to record the relative humidity (RH). The sensitivity of 0.193dB/%RH was obtained and the measurement range of relative humidity is between 25% and 80%.

articleTitle: Time-domain channel estimation for polarization interleaving OFDM-PON
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose an efficient time-domain channel estimation method for polarization interleaving orthogonal frequency division multiplexing passive optical network (OFDM-PON) with direct detection. Compared with the frequency-domain least square channel estimator (FLSE) and intra-symbol frequency-domain averaging (ISFA), the time-domain channel estimator (TD-CE) with overhead reduction demonstrates better system robustness against transmission impairments, such as optical noise, chromatic dispersion, and polarization mode dispersion.

articleTitle: Trapping of microparticles with microfiber enhanced by Sagnac interferometer
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a method of trapping micro-particles with microfiber enhanced by Sagnac interferometer. The microfiber waist diameter is 2.24µm. It is single mode fiber and has relatively large evanescent wave when it works in the water based suspension with wave length of 1550nm. The amplitude of the stationary wave formed in Sagnac interferometer is enhanced. The particles trapping ability with the crest of the stationary wave is increased either. This particles trapping experiment is carried out with light power of about milli-watt and 1µm polystyrene microsphere. Micro-particles could be trapped in a quasi-static state.

articleTitle: Polarization Mode Dispersion monitoring for phase-modulated optical signals utilizing parallel cross-phase modulation in a highly nonlinear fiber
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a first-order Polarization Mode Dispersion (PMD) monitoring technique for phase-modulated optical signals utilizing the cross-phase modulation (XPM) effect between the input signal and the inserted continuous-wave probe in parallel connection. Because of accumulation of PMD, the XPM effect in nonlinear fiber leads to variation of pump phase. This can cause spectrum broadening resulting in variation of pump power. The technique can suppress the influence of PMD in one branch of the two signals in parallel connection then use the difference of the two pump power at the same band to monitor PMD. The simulation shows that the technique can monitor PMD of 40-Gb/s non-return-to-zero differential quadrature phase-shift keying (NRZ-DQPSK) from 0-30ps.The dynamic range over 3dB can be used in accurate monitoring compared to existing methods. The applicability of this monitoring technique to higher bit-rate phase-modulated signals, such as 80-Gb/s NRZ-DQPSK, is also investigated via simulation.

articleTitle: Quaternion approach to study of the polarization maintaining optical fibers
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, the progress of the stress sensor based on Polarization Maintaining Fiber (PMF) is reviewed, and point out that the joint multi-effect of internal and external effects in PMF based sensor is a basic phenomenon, and the study on multi-effect have important academic value and application prospects. A quaternion approach to study on the multi-effects of PMF sensor is proposed, and the cosines law on the multi-effects is presented and proved. Theoretical analysis and simulation based on the theorem are given. The experiments to demonstrate the multi-effect is designed and related results proved the correctness of the cosines law of joint multi-effect.

articleTitle: Polarization-relevance noise compensation for an Φ-OTDR based optical communication network maintenance system
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Optical network is the backbone of modern data communication. The relevant maintenance technologies are of fundamental importance if the reliability of optical communication network is required. However, traditional monitoring and diagnosing methods such as the Rayleigh back-scattering (RBS) based optical time-domain reflectometry (OTDR) and coherent OTDR (COTDR) are only suitable for static measurement. That means they cannot make early warning before serious failure is actually occurred. Recently, phase-sensitive OTDR (Φ-OTDR) has attracted more and more attentions for its high sensitivity and distributed vibration detection ability. Monitoring technology based on Φ-OTDR could capture disturbance event through vibrating field, which can preserve the optical communication fibre from being destroyed even when the threat event has not directly contacted with the network yet. Unfortunately, those installed telecommunication fibres have small but significant birefringence. Once any of the disturbance events leads to a local birefringence change, the polarization evolution of the Rayleigh back-scattering signal will be disturbed along the following fibre, which will result in the generation of polarization-relevance noise (PRN) and the failure of multi-point vibration events identification. An orthogonal-SOP pulse pair (OSPP) method has been proposed to compensate the polarization-dependence of Φ-OTDR, making the sensing technology purely phase-sensitive. Experimental result has shown that a noise suppression ratio of 8.2dB could be achieved. The proposed method can reduce PRN influence on Φ-OTDR without complicating the sensor scheme, which extends the potential of Φ-OTDR technology in optical communication network maintenance system.

articleTitle: Nanosoldering of hetero-structures consisting of silver nanowires and gold nanoplate for interconnect
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate plasmonic nanosoldering of hetero-materials and hetero-structures including two silver NWs and a gold nanoplate is also demonstrated to verify the universality of this technique. Since these nanostructures are building blocks for composing plasmonic integrated circuits, this study will benefit the development of nanowire-related plasmonic or electric interconnect.

articleTitle: Design of information pushing system based on visible light communication
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The design of information pushing system based on visible light communication (VLC) and its optical channel performance testing were presented. The system was designed to meet requirements of some intensive conferences or special security area. The results showed that the transmission bandwidth of video signal was 500Kbps. Besides, data transmission rate of 4Mbit/s at the distance of 2.5m was achieved 7 levels of light dimming and the 3Mbit/s of data transmission were implemented simultaneously without interference by amplifying the NRZ-OOK signal. By Manchester encoding, the video signal of system could be transmitted without bit error under 1 m free space transmission length.

articleTitle: Development of optical fibre humidity sensors for assessing the quality of housing insulation materials
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A fibre optic-based relative humidity (RH) sensing system has been developed for assessing the qualities of housing insulation materials, based on a Polyimide (PI)-coated Fibre Bragg Grating (FBG) device. This forms the key moisture sensitive element, allowing a carefully-designed and packaged sensor system to be fabricated, evaluated and calibrated, creating the robustness and reusability needed. Following calibration, the system performance evaluated on a range of commercial housing insulation materials shows excellent performance in establishing the key moisture-transport parameters of the materials routinely used by structural engineers. Cross-sensitivity issues are addressed allowing the RH sensor system to operate over a wide range of RH level experienced normally in this application. A sensitivity of 1.1 pm/%RH, with low hysteresis from a ruggedized sensor, is observed.

articleTitle: Fiber refractive index sensor based on Surface Plasmon Resonance in triangular pyramid structure
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A refractive index (RI) sensor based on Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) in triangular pyramid structures is proposed. The sensor is fabricated by a silver coated triangular pyramid structure at the end of single-mode fiber. We analyze the effect of the thickness of the metal layer using numerical simulations. The theoretical results show that triangular pyramid structures can effectively stimulate the Surface Plasmon Wave (SPW), and a good transmission dip can be obtained when the silver film thickness is between 30 to 40 nm. According to the numerical simulation results, when the thickness of the film is 30nm, the average sensitivity can reach 2590 nm/RIU in the RI range of 1.33–1.41.

articleTitle: 2.2GHz mode locked all-fiber Erbium doped laser based on a tilted fiber grating
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: By incorporating a 45° tilted grating in a fiber laser cavity with net anomalous dispersion, we have obtained stable soliton pulses with a high repetition. The laser could operate at high harmonics of the fundamental repetition frequency of the resonator (22.6 MHz) by properly adjusting the polarization controllers in the cavity. The highest achieved repetition rate is 2.2 GHz which corresponds to the 97<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> harmonic order.

articleTitle: Single mode fibers for cascaded higher-order soliton compression
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Detailed fiber design of single mode fibers for two-stage higher-order soliton compression at 1550 nm is presented for the first time. A compression factor of 87.8 has been achieved.

articleTitle: Large slow light capacity in graphene-based grating waveguide
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We have systematically investigated the slow light performances based on two-dimensional material graphene, giving the conclusion that graphene exhibits much larger slow light capability than other materials. A large delay-bandwidth product has been obtained in a simple yet functional graphene-based waveguide with slow down factor c / υ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub> at 109 and slow light bandwidth Δω at 14.5 nm, which is several orders of magnitude larger than previous results.

articleTitle: Timing phase estimation using nonlinear preprocessing for coherent optical systems with Nyquist and FTN signaling
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a feed-forward timing phase estimation scheme that requires only two samples per symbol for coherent optical transport systems with Nyquist/FTN signaling. Simulation results confirm that the proposed scheme has similar performance to conventional algorithms using four samples per symbol.

articleTitle: Tunable V-cavity laser based transmitter optical sub-assembly with a wavelength locker
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A wavelength locker is designed and fabricated for a V-cavity laser (VCL) based transmitter optical sub-assembly (TOSA). The tunable VCL and the wavelength locker are packaged together into a small-form-factor 20-pin TOSA box, which is only about 4.4 × 9.5mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and an electronic driver is developed for wavelength tuning and locker control. The frequency of the laser is stabilized within ±0.1GHz, and the response time of the locker control is about 4s.

articleTitle: Single-wavelength 100Gb/s and 200Gb/s transmissions over 80km SMF based on direct detection eSSB-DMT and Twin-SSB-DMT
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Base on a DDMZM, we propose and demonstrate a 100-Gb/s system for 80km SMF transmission using direct-detection eSSB-DMT. Furthermore, a twin-SSB-DMT is realized based on the same transmitter architecture and 200Gb/s over 80km SMF is successfully demonstrated with novel receiver and MIMO-array DSP.

articleTitle: Novel optical fiber Bragg grating designs for vector bending measurement
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Two novel fiber Bragg grating (FBG) based sensing schemes are proposed and experimentally demonstrated for directional bending measurement: One of which is based on two weakly titled Bragg gratings spliced together with tilt planes at nearly 90 degree, followed by a cleaved end mirror; the other one is based on an off-axis printed FBG, which both exhibit large amount of cladding modes in transmission spectrum in contrast with that of a normal FBG. Well-chosen cladding resonances in these two structure are demonstrated respectively for ultra-sensitive bending measurement via power detection. Meanwhile the surrounding temperature is proven independent to fiber bent.

articleTitle: A high-sensitivity microfluidic flowmeter based on microfiber coupler
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we utilize a microfiber coupler (MFC) to realize the measurement of the microfluidic flow rate. A glass capillary is chosen as the microfluidic channel. The capillary is coated with gold film. The MFC is wrapped around the gold film which is to heat the device. One kind of UV adhesive is selected to package the device and isolate it from the ambient. The flow rate of the microfluidics is determined by the wavelength shift of the MFC. The flowmeter shows a very high sensitivity of 0.82 nm/(μl/s) when the microfluidic flow rate is 1 μl/s.

articleTitle: Formation of long period microfiber gratings with higher-order diffraction by arc discharge method
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Long period gratings (LPGs) inscribed in microfibers have potential applications in wide wavelength-tunable filters, communications, and sensors (e.g., for detection of refractive index and other biochemical parameters). In this work, we propose higher-order diffraction microfiber LPGs, fabricated by use of electric arc-discharge technique for the first time, to our knowledge. A program is developed to realize it. A series of samples with grating periods of 400µm, 500µm, 600µm, 800µm, and 1000µm in association with different diffraction orders are realized. The arc-induced LPGs exhibit high refractive index sensitivity and low temperature cross-sensitivity, showing great potential for the sensing applications.

articleTitle: Gamma radiation impact on performance of DPSK based inter-satellite optical communication system
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: DPSK based inter-satellite optical communication systems are exposed to space radiation environment. As the component of radiation environment, gamma irradiation will result in serious system performance degradation. In order to analyze the performance degradation, main devices employed in a DPSK based inter-satellite optical communication system were irradiated to a total dose of 10krad with the dose rate of 5rad/s using a Co<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</sup> radiation source. Gamma irradiation impacts on devices were analyzed and on the basis, system performance degradation was simulated. BER was analyzed as a function of gamma radiation dose at laser transmitter and receiver. In addition, according to simulation results, we deemed that it is necessary to improve the radiation hardness of EDFA and laser transmitter so as to enhance system performance against gamma radiation.

articleTitle: Sol-gel silica coated optical fiber sensor for ammonia gas detection
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A high sensitivity ammonia gas sensor based on a tapered small core single-mode fiber (SCSMF) structure for measurement of ammonia gas concentration is reported. The proposed tapered SCSMF fiber structure has a waist diameter of 13.5 μm and it is fabricated using a customized microheater brushing technique. The silica based material prepared by sol-gel method is used as a coating applied to the surface of tapered fiber structures. Experimental results show that sensor is very sensitive to ammonia. The best measurement resolution of the ammonia concentration is estimated to be 16 ppb for gas concentrations of 0.5 ppm to 2.5 ppm while the response and recovery times are less than 5 and 10 minutes respectively.

articleTitle: Spread spectrum-based white light communication with experiments
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper a Direct Sequence Spread Spectrum (DSSS) based offline wireless white light communication system is established. Field measurements are conducted to compare the performance with and without DSSS. The experimental results show that the DSSS is able to improve performance obviously.

articleTitle: Intravascular Frequency-domain optical coherence tomography imaging system
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We present a Frequency-domain optical coherence tomography (FD-OCT) system for intravascular imaging. The whole system consists of 4 parts: imaging catheter (IC), motion controller (MC), optical engine (OE) and data acquisition and processing module (DAPM). By using swept laser source with 50 KHz sweep speed and high speed optical rotary jiont, we can get 100 frames per second (fps) and scan 20 mm vessel per second.

articleTitle: An SDH off-line signal analysis software based on LabVIEW
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: SDH(Synchronous Digital Hierarchy) is one of the hot technology in optical fiber communication which has the large capacity and high data transmission rate, and it uses block frame structure to carry information. In this paper, a method of analyzing the structure of SDH frame by an off-line signal analysis software based on LabVIEW is presented. And this paper describes the implementation of lead-lag PLL(phase locked loop) in LabVIEW, which is the key technology used in the process of clock and data recovery.

articleTitle: 20.1-W, b-cut Tm,Ho:YAlO3 laser pumped by two laser diodes
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A 20.1 W, continuous wave (CW) operation of a b-cut Tm, Ho:YAlO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> (Tm,Ho:YAP) laser at 2.12 μm is reported in this paper. The Tm,Ho:YAP crystal, which was cooled by liquid nitrogen at 77 K, was double end-pumped by two 22.5-W fiber-coupled laser diodes at 794.3 nm. An optical-optical conversion efficiency of 44.7% was achieved, corresponding to a slope efficiency of 46.1%.

articleTitle: A dual-parameter active fibre sensor based on modal interference in few-mode fibres
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a dual-parameter active fibre sensor based on a fibre ring laser using a single-mode-two-mode-single-mode (STS) fibre interferemeter and a four-mode FBG as the intracavity dual-parameter sensing element. The interferometric spectra of the STS are investigated with different core-offset parameters and few-mode fibre length. The highest LP11 mode excitation ratio is achieved with a 6μm core-offset distance in the STS which achieves best sensing ability. High precision dual-parameter sensing of pressure and tension are achieved experimentally by measurements of fibre laser output wavelength and intensity.

articleTitle: Two-bit bit-flipping algorithm for decoding low-density parity-check codes based on syndrome weight
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a novel two-bit bit-flipping (BF) decoding algorithm is proposed for low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes. The proposed algorithm flips two bits per iteration based on the syndrome-weight metric. Since the algorithm requires only logical operations during the iterations. The proposed tow-bit BF algorithm has low complexity. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm has faster convergence speed and about 0.2 dB gain compared to standard BF decoding algorithm.

articleTitle: Proposal for distributed measurement of Müller matrix in optical fibers
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We present a proposal for distributed measurement of Müller matrix with single-polarized probing light in the optical fiber. The physical principle and corresponding mathematical treatment on the propagation of Rayleigh backscattering light is investigated. Through numerical analysis, it can be demonstrated that the distribution of Müller matrix in the fiber can be acquired with the proposed method. This work may have significant potential in polarization-dependent distributed fiber-optic sensing.

articleTitle: Direct-modulated multiple formats optical OFDM system based on Discrete Wavelet Transform
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrated a direct-modulated multiple formats optical OFDM system based on Discrete Wavelet Transform by using MATLAB software. The simulation results indicated that DWT-OFDM has a good advantage over FFT-OFDM, and the signals at a bit rate 5Gbit/s have a good performance which is nearly equal to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> when OSNR is equal to 25dB over 300km optical fiber channel which only concerns the influence of chromatic dispersion.

articleTitle: On chip broadband microwave photonics phase shifter based on the coupling-modulated microring resonator
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a microwave photonics phase shifter which utilizes a coupling-modulated microring resonator (CMR) with interleaved p-n junctions. The transmission response of the CMR can be tuned by changing the effect coupling factor through applying bias voltage on the feedback arm. Finally, 1 V bias voltage is chosen to apply on the CMR. A microwave photonics phase shifter with phase shift range of 120 degree from 15 GHz to 40 GHz and the RF power variation less than 5 dBm is realized.

articleTitle: Dissipative soliton resonance pulse generation from an all-fiber mode-locked dumbbell-shaped fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report on a new design for a passively mode-locked dumbbell-shaped fiber laser employing all normal dispersion fibers at 1 μm. The laser produced pulses of 18.8 nJ and 42.4 nJ from two output ports, at a repetition rate of 7.19 MHz. A narrow bandpass filter is inserted into the laser cavity to achieve the dissipative soliton resonance pulse generation.

articleTitle: Space radiation effects on optical fiber communication links and design suggestions
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Optical fibre communication technology is relative new to satellite application over the world. The mechanism of damaged induced by space radiation effects has been analysed on fibre links, and some achievements of research abroad have been presented. For optical transceiver, we completed a series of single particle experiments, which help us to find most sensitive components of fibre links for SEE. Based on test results, this paper provides several design suggestions to improve reliability for space fiber communication system, which can be referenced by satellite system designation for various space missions.

articleTitle: Static/dynamic strain interrogations of FBG sensor based on radio frequency unbalanced M-Z interferometer
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The operation of a novel radio-frequency unbalanced M-Z interferometer is demonstrated for strain interrogation on FBG sensor, which can simultaneously achieve static and dynamic strain sensing with high accuracy.

articleTitle: Analysis on spatial and temporal resolution in photonic time stretch frequency domain reflectometry based fully distributed fiber Bragg grating sensors
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose and experimentally demonstrate fully distributed strain sensing along the length of a linearly chirped fibre Bragg grating with simultaneously high spatial and temporal resolution based on photonic time stretch frequency domain reflectometry (PTS-FDR). The distributed strain information is reconstructed from the instantaneous RF frequency of a temporal interference waveform via short-time Fourier transform analysis. The utility of the proposed method is characterized by analysing the spatial and temporal resolution obtained. An ultrafast strain measurement at a speed of 50 MHz with a high spatial resolution of 31.5 µm over a gauge length of 25 mm and a strain resolution of 9.1 µε have been achieved.

articleTitle: Low cost optical fiber sensing system based on low coherence interferometers for temperature and strain multiplexed measurement
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Fiber optical sensors based on low-coherence interferometerer have been widely researched in recent years since its high precision and wide measuring range. For commercial application, we demonstrated such a system which consists of two low-coherence interferometer and a data acquisition card for measurement in the field of temperature and strain. By testing the interference signal influenced by temperature and strain variation, the sensitivity of 12 μm/°C and 0.16 μm/με were obtained.

articleTitle: Application research of Raman thermometer on quality evaluating of fiber coil
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Fiber coil is a kind of key optical component used in fiber optic gyroscope, and its stability and anti-jamming capability directly influence the performance of the whole fiber optic gyroscope. The quadrupolar winding of fiber coil can restrain thermally induced nonreciprocity obviously at ideal conditions; however, various nonideal factors severely limit the advantage of the quadrupolar winding. A novel method for analyzing the quality of the fiber coil using Raman temperature measurement technology is proposed. The nonreciprocity of fiber coil can be judged by analyzing Raman scattering of fiber coil under conditions of varying temperature, and then the quality of winding a coil can be judged. The corresponding experiments have been done to verify the effect this new method. The results show that this non-destructive method has a guiding role to the fiber coil winding method and technology, and also provide a way for evaluating the quality of the fiber coil.

articleTitle: Up to 100-Gbps single lambda PAM4 generation by dual-drive Mach-Zehnder modulator and transmission over 5-Km SSMF
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this work, 4-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM4) by using commercial dual-drive Mach-Zehnder Modulator (DD-MZM) is experimentally investigated. We have demonstrated the generation of PAM4 signal up to 50 Gbaud (100 Gbps). The transmission of the PAM4 signal over 5-Km standard single mode fiber (SSMF) is achieved with error-free below the FEC limit (3.8E-3), without employing digital equalization at 90 Gbps. The linear-amplifier-free configuration by DD-MZM leads to simplified implementation and improved performance for high speed PAM4 signal generation, which would be of great significance for short reach optical interconnection.

articleTitle: Refractive index sensitivity of photonic crystal fiber with a graphene-coating gold layer
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel LCPCF-SPR sensor with a graphene-coating gold layer is reported with a larger wavelength difference between phase matching point and propagation loss peak. It also shows coexistence of positive/negative RI sensitivity.

articleTitle: Optical fiber humidity sensor based On PVA-coated M-Z interferometer
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A relative humidity sensor by using a Mach-Zehnder interferometer in a standard single mode fiber (SMF) with two waist-enlarged tapers is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. It is fabricated by waist-enlarged splicing a section of SMF between two SMFs. A thin layer of 5% polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) is dip-coated onto SMF and two tapers. With the increase of relative humidity, the resonance wavelength peak shifts towards longer wavelength. The sensitivity of the relative humidity measurement of 0.09883nm/%RH in the range from 40% to 90%RH is experimentally achieved. The temperature effect of the proposed relative humidity sensor is also analyzed.

articleTitle: Dual-valley transmission spectrum based on periodically poled lithium niobate with a structure defect
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We observe the symmetrical dual-valley spectrum in periodically poled lithium niobate (PPLN) with a defect in the middle employing electro-optic effect. When the external electric fields are applied, light satisfying phase-matching condition (λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>) will undergo polarization rotation and then turn back. However, the polarization states of wavelength at λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>±Δλ will be changed at the end of the sample due to phase mismatching. A dual-valley transmission spectrum is thus obtained. Moreover, the depth of the valley could be tailored with different electric fields on the y-surface of the sample.

articleTitle: High power linearly polarized narrow linewidth ytterbium doped fiber laser at 1120 nm
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Based on spectral symmetric cavity with respect to fiber Bragg gratings bandwidth, a 1120 nm narrow linewidth ytterbium-doped-fiber laser is demonstrated. A maximum output power of 14.67 W is obtained corresponding to an optical efficiency of 63.5 %. The measured center wavelength of the output laser is 1118.7 nm with a linewidth as narrow as 0.08 nm. The gain of the laser is more than 60dB above the ASE, and the polarization extinction ratio is 19.8 dB. As far as we are aware, this is the highest optical efficiency, largest ASE suppression, and narrowest linewidth reported from cladding pumped linearly polarized 1120nm fiber lasers.

articleTitle: VoIP reconstruction via sparse linear prediction
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: With the development of network and speech coding, various applications of transmitting voice over internet protocol (VoIP) come into our lives. Speech reconstruction is required, as the packet loss caused by the real-time constraints transmission protocols results in the loss of speech segments. The paper proposes a novel approach to addressing speech reconstruction problem utilizing a high-order sparse linear predictor. This predictor is able to maintain the high sparsity level involved by the classical speech model as much as possible. Then we adopt differential evolution algorithm, which is arguably one of the most powerful stochastic real-parameter optimization algorithms, to predict the sparse coefficients and missing speech segments simultaneously. Experiments show the superior performance of this new approach in both signal to noise ratio (SNR) and perceptual evaluation of speech quality (PESQ).

articleTitle: Study on characteristics of U-shaped fiber Bragg gratings on wet etching properties
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A new evanescent field sensor is described based on a U-shaped fiber Bragg gratings (FBGs) structure, and sensitized by a hydrofluoric (HF)-etching treatment, and their spectral evolution under HF-etching has been studied. Experimental results indicate that the wavelength shifts toward shorter wavelength faster as the bending curvature of the FBGs increases under HF-Etching. Moreover, there are some reflective peaks in reflection spectrum when FBG is bent after HF-etching treatment. The results show the transition behaviors of FBGs from normal to tilted structures when they are bent and etched. Meanwhile, U-shaped structure would enhance the mechanical strength of the fibers.

articleTitle: Refractive index sensor based on thin-core microfiber
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The refractive index sensor is fabricated by tapering a thin-core-fiber (TCF) and sandwiched between two segments of standard single-mode fibers. For the TCMF with a diameter of 30 μm and taper length of 18 mm, a maximum sensitivity of 2459.18 nm/RIU has been experimentally achieved for a RI range of 1.4237 to 1.4335 and the detection limit is about 2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> RIU. This photonic device has excellent RI sensing property, which is expected to be applied in biological, chemical areas, as well as the application as tunable photonic device.

articleTitle: Research of clustering and group leader election algorithm on hierarchy Ad Hoc Network
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Tactical Networks is typical Ad Hoc Network. Its structure leads to relative fixation for hierarchy and clustering. In order to maintain the cluster stabilization and network function in particular cases, Group leader election can be reached by address list message and connectedness message.

articleTitle: 1.90-W, 7.06-µm ZnGeP2 optical parametric oscillators pumped by a 2.05-µm laser
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report a tunable mid-infrared optical parametric oscillator (OPO) using a single ZnGeP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> (ZGP) crystal with the cut-angle of 51.4°. A 17.0-W Q-switch Tm,Ho:GdVO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> laser is pumped by 800-nm LDs to generate 2.05-μm radiation, which have been used for pumping a angle-tuned ZGP OPO to generate mid-IR tunable from 5.84 to 7.87 μm. A 1.90-W idler output power has been acquired at 7.06 μm with 17.0-W pump power, corresponding to the idler laser slope efficiency of 13.4 %.

articleTitle: Dynamic bandwidth management based on classification of traffic in software-defined WDM-TDM PON architecture
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Passive Optical Network (PON) is the most promising technology in optical access network, and the effective and reasonable upstream dynamic bandwidth allocation (DBA) is the key. This paper proposes a new software defined WDM-TDM PON frame that enable more users to share a single high-capacity fiber access as well as introduce a flexible DBA module to replace the hardware-configured DBA module. The simulation result shows that the delay is reduced up to 23% and the software-defined PON can meet the different priority traffic of QoS in comparison with traditional PON.

articleTitle: High order Bragg gratings for short wavelengths operation
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: High order gratings using phase mask technique are investigated theoretically and experimentally. The results shows that even a small amount of the zeroth-order component in the diffraction distribution would have substantial effects on high order gratings. It provides a useful basis for producing different gratings towards short wavelength application using one single phase mask.

articleTitle: Wavelength tuning and bound states of dissipative solitons in fiber lasers
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report an experimental observation of wavelength tuning and bound states of solitons in the same fiber laser. Through adopting the Mach-Zehnder interferometer as an intra-cavity tunable filter, continuously wavelength-tunable operation from 1553.0 nm to 1565.0 nm is achieved. Additionally with modest polarization manipulation, bound states of solitons with switchable wavelengths and different pulse separations are also observed.

articleTitle: A temperature sensor based on topological insulators and tapered fiber
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A temperature sensor based on topological insulators and tapered fiber is proposed and experimentally investigated. The tapered fiber and topological insulators solution are encapsulated in a capillary tube using UV glue. Within a temperature range of 47–92 centigrade, one resonance dip of tapered fiber exhibits a blue shift of 10nm, which is more than 20 times of ordinary fiber Bragg grating's temperature sensitivity.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of 25-Gbit/s data information transfer over a 2-km orbital angular momentum (OAM) fiber link based on amplitude-to-OAM modulation mapping
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate 25 Gbit/s data transmission over a 2-km orbital angular momentum (OAM) fiber link based on amplitude-to-OAM mode modulation mapping, and achieve bit-error rate (BER) below 3.8e-3.
