articleTitle: Surface plasmon resonance based on multi-angel tilted fiber Bragg grating for highly sensitive and wide range refractive index measurement
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Surface-plasmon resonance (SPR), which results from the strong sensitivity of the plasmon-propagation constant to the permittivity of a nanoscale layer of material on a metal surface, is an exquisitely sensitive technique to detect chemical and biochemical changes occurring between molecules. In this work, we propose and demonstrate an SPR sensor based on a multi-angle tilted fiber Bragg grating (TFBG) coated by a 50 nm-thickness gold film for refractive index (RI) measurement. Experimental results show that wide range of RI, from 1.15 to 1.43, can be detected using the proposed SPR sensor, with sensitivity of 523.41 nm/RIU (refractive index unit). In addition, with designed as a probe, through coating a gold film as a reflection mirror in the cleaved end downstream of the grating, the length of the entire sensor is only 2 cm, making it easy to insert into the media for biochemical measurements.

articleTitle: Bitrate flexible transceivers based on IMDD half-cycle subcarrier M-QAM for software-defined optical access networks
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a bitrate flexible optical transceiver scheme for software-defined optical access networks by means of half-cycle subcarrier M-QAM using intensity modulation and direct detection. Here, the transceivers can successfully generate four different modulation formats at 20, 40, 50, 60 Gb/s using MATLAB program and receive without changing the hardware platform. Simulation results show that the 10GBaud signals are successfully transmitted over 30-km-SMF with electronic dispersion compensation.

articleTitle: Characteristic analysis of atmospheric turbulence from inland to ocean
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Random fluctuation of turbulence brings random fluctuation of refractive index, which makes atmosphere become a random fluctuation medium and destroys the coherence of light wave especially laser transferring in it. Exploration of atmospheric turbulence is essentially investigation of atmospheric refractive index. The atmospheric structure constant of refractive index is a basic parameter of expressing atmospheric turbulence, and is measured using HTP-2 micro-thermal meter at different areas from inland to ocean. It is analysed that the relation of atmospheric structure constant of refractive index with corresponding temperature and wind speed. The conclusion of developing law of turbulence and main influencing factors is to deepen the research in atmospheric optical transmission, and to provide data support for the siting of ship board photoelectric systems.

articleTitle: A novel scattered pilot-aided channel compensation for CO-OFDM systems
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a channel compensation method with a novel structure of scattered pilots for coherent optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (CO-OFDM) systems including linear fiber dispersion effects and noises from optical amplifiers. Simulation results over a range of Optical Signal to Noise Ratios (OSNRs) with use of scattered pilots for both conventional and proposed methods are shown. The proposed method can achieve high spectral efficiency and a better performance in Bit Error Rate (BER) compared with the conventional scattered method.

articleTitle: Optical transmission system board fault diagnosis based on fault tree
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Traditional fault diagnosis of optical transmission system board mainly relies on experience, resulting in lack of common fault diagnosis method. In response to this, PQ1 board of OptiX2500+ optical transmission system is selected as a research object. After principle analyzing and fault tree analysis, a fault tree model is constructed, which can be used in fault diagnosis and maintenance. Several diagnosis examples are adopted to validate the fault tree. The result indicates that it is efficient, reliable and accurate.

articleTitle: Supercontinuum generation with a wavelength tunable passively mode-locked Yb-doped fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We proposed a supercontinuum all-fiber laser, by tuning the wavelength of the pump source, a series of different output spectra with different wavelength ranges were obtained at same output power. By analyzing the spectral characteristics of the generated supercontinuum, the zero-dispersion wavelength of the photonic crystal fiber in the laser can be deduced.

articleTitle: Experimental research on passively Q-switched Yb:YAG Microchip Lasers with A Nd,Cr:YAG as saturable absorber
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We experimentally investigate a diode-pumped passively Q-switched Yb:YAG laser with a Nd,Cr:YAG as saturable absorber. The minimum pulse width of 52ns is obtained, and the maximum of average power is 770mW. The repetition rate of the pulse train increases with the pump power increasing. The maximum of repetition is 3.6kHz.

articleTitle: Temperature-insensitive optical strain sensor based on interlaced tilted phase-shifted long-period fiber grating
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A new type of interlaced tilted phase-shifted long period grating (IPLPG) has been fabricated using focused CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser. For the axial strain and temperature, the two resonance dips produced by phase-shift have different features. They have obvious differences for axial strain which are −5.0522×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−4</sup> nm/µε and -7.9767×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−4</sup> nm/µε from 340µε to 3060µε.

articleTitle: Capacity improvement by adaptive bit-loading and Volterra filtering in a DML-based IM/DD system
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a 36-Gb/s DMT signal transmission over 50-km SSMF based on a cost-effective 10-GHz DML-based IM/DD system. The data rate is improved by 22% with Volterra filtering.

articleTitle: Compact continuous wave optical parametric amplifier for tunable 1.44–1.50 µm laser radiation
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate an all-fiber optical parametric amplifier (OPA) for generating widely tunable 1.44-1.50 μm laser. The OPA is achieved by simultaneously injecting a continuous wave (CW) 1533.4 nm fiber laser and a tunable laser into a 2-km long highly nonlinear fiber (HNF). Idler wave of 1439.98 nm wavelength with low threshold of 13.62 mW and narrow bandwidth of 0.1 nm is obtained in the experiment. By varying the lasing wavelength of the tunable laser from 1639.8 to 1564.8 nm, the wavelength of generated idler wave can be widely tuned from 1439.98 to 1503.20 nm. Such OPA provides a simple and accessible scheme for generating tunable 1.44-1.50 μm fiber laser source.

articleTitle: A compact design of 1310 nm high gain high power hybrid fiber amplifier
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We construct a high gain high output power 1310 nm hybrid fiber amplifier, which can be use in telecommunication. It is a compact design combining a semiconductor optical amplifier (SOA) and a discrete Raman amplifier. It is hard to construct such amplifier by either using a SOA or a discrete Raman fiber amplifier with compact design. The amplifier is designed for a 1310 nm small signal input providing a high gain, and high output power with fast response.

articleTitle: Energy saving Algorithms based on wavelength migration in Time and Wavelength Division Multiplexed Passive Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Time and Wavelength Division Multiplexed Passive Access Network (TWDM-PON) can support 40Gb/s transmission rate, which has become a hot research topic. Due to the bandwidth flexibility, wavelength flexibility and multiple users' access, it is imperative to optimize network resources, improve the transmission rate meanwhile reduce network energy consumption. This paper has proposed two optimization algorithms which reduce the working wavelengths number as far as possible and then put off the idle wavelengths, so as to reduce the network energy consumption. In addition, the proposed two algorithms can also improve the bandwidth utilization of wavelengths. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithms can effectively reduce the network energy consumption and improve the bandwidth utilization.

Author Keywords: Time and Wavelength-Division Multiplexed Passive Access Network

articleTitle: High speed dense wavelength division multiplexing atmospheric laser communication system
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrated a high speed atmospheric laser communication system based on a two channels dense wavelength division multiplexing, and 10Gb/s non return to zero sequence and 10GHz sine wave are modulated on the channels respectively. The channel spacing is 100GHz and the experimental distance is over 1km. The experimental results show that this dense wavelength division multiplexing system can realize the high speed information atmospheric transmission.

articleTitle: A waveband routing method in Elastic Optical Networks based on the Tandem Structure Hierarchical Optical Cross-Connect
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Based on the Tandem Structure Hierarchical Optical Cross-Connect (TS-HOXC), an Integer Linear Programming (ILP) formulation is presented and solved for route, spectrum, and waveband assignment (RSBA) in a waveband switched elastic optical network (WS-EON). Simulation results show that this WS-EON is almost as spectrally efficient as an EON using single-layer OXCs but uses substantially fewer optical switch ports.

articleTitle: Experimental study of a 2×2 MIMO scheme for ultraviolet communications
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a MIMO ultraviolet (UV) communication system which can increase the data rate effectively. The bit error rate (BER) performance of a 2×2 MIMO scheme is measured and analyzed by offline experiments.

articleTitle: Temperature and Refractive index sensor based on an etched thin core fiber
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel fiber in-line Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) is demonstrated for temperature and refractive index measurements. The sensor is formed by splicing a section of etched thin core fiber (TCF) between two single mode fibers (SMFs). Experimental results show that, high temperature sensitivity of 198.5pm/°C with a temperature variation of 40°C is achieved. The Refractive index (RI) response of the sensor is also investigated; the RI sensitivity is up to -66.305 nm/RIU within the RI range of 1.3286 - 1.3668.

articleTitle: Parallel coupled filter based on spoof surface plasmon polaritons
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Parallel coupled filter based on spoof surface plasmon polaritons is presented in this letter. Designed on a thin dielectric substrate, the ultrathin metallic structure is composed of rectangle drilled hole metal strip. A planar spoof SPPs parallel coupled resonator has been integrated into the drilled hole metallic strip to produce narrow. We simulate the parallel coupled filter in microwave frequency band. The simulate results show that the filter has two narrow pass-band, the equivalent relative bandwidth (6.8%), the central frequency (5.9 GHz), the insertion loss is above −3dB in the passband from 5.7 to 6.1 GHz, and the equivalent relative bandwidth (2.3%), the central frequency (17.1GHz), the insertion loss is above −3dB in the passband from 16.9 to 17.3GHz. Due to planar structures proposed here, it is easy to integrate in the microwave integrated systems, which can play an important role in the microwave communication circuit and system.

articleTitle: Compensation for transceiver IQ mismatch with phase noise in CO-OFDM system
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a simultaneous compensation method to against transmitter (Tx) and receiver (Rx) in-phase/quadrature (IQ) mismatch is proposed in the presence of phase noise originating from the transmitter and local oscillator (LO) lasers for coherent optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (CO-OFDM) system. A mathematical model is given which includes the transceiver IQ mismatch and laser phase noise above mentioned. Based on the given model, a recursive algorithm is offered, in which the compensated results are updated symbol by symbol. Simulation results show that when the Tx and Rx amplitude mismatch are2dB, phase mismatch are 10° and 5°, a 1.2dB optical signal-to noise ratio is improved for 60kHz of the laser linewidth of the proposed method by compared with the hybrid method.

articleTitle: 3D-DMONoC: A new topology for Optical Network on Chip
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Optical Network on Chip (ONoC) is an emerging communication architecture since it can potentially offer ultrahigh bandwidth and low latency to multiprocessor systems. With the increasing number of IP cores integrated on a single chip, the design of 3-Dimensional (3D) ONoC has salient strengths in terms of area and cost. Here, a novel 3D ONoC architecture with two layers named 3D Diagonally-Shifted Mesh ONoC (3D-DMONoC) is proposed. Accordingly, two original switching elements with simple structure are put forward to simplify traditional 7×7 optical routers in 3D ONoCs. Accompanied with the employment of wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) technology and wavelength routing scheme, 3D-DMONoC achieves at-most-once turning for the optical signal and avoids wavelength conversion for the communication between any two nodes. The evaluation and simulation results show that the saturation load is improved more than 1.7 times and the saving in the number of microring resonators (MRs) reaches 81.96% at most compared with prior ONoCs.

articleTitle: MIMO visible light communications system using imaging receiver with angle diversity detectors
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We present and evaluate a multiple-input multiple-output visible light communications (MIMO-VLC) system using imaging angle diversity receiver (ImADR). Differing from the conventional imaging receiver (ImR), which has a two-dimensional circular detector array consisting of vertically oriented detectors, the ImADR has a three-dimensional spherical-cap-shaped detector array composed of angle diversity detectors. Compared with ImR, ImADR has a wider field-of-view and a smaller area of detector array. Our studies show that a 4×4 MIMO-VLC system employing ImADR can increase the communication coverage by about 130% at a target bit error rate of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>, compared with the system employing the conventional ImR.

articleTitle: M-Z optical fiber liquid level sensor based on two cascaded spherical-shape structures
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An MZI for measurement of liquid level is proposed and demonstrated, which consists of two cascaded spherical-shape structures. Two interferometers with different lengths of 34mm and 40mm are manufactured with their sensing characteristics studied. By measuring wavelength shifts of the dip in the interference spectrum, we can measurement liquid level. Experimental results show that the sensor (34mm) has a higher sensitivity of liquid level compared to the sensor (40mm). A higher liquid level sensitivity of -1.172nm/cm is obtained.

articleTitle: Regenerator sharing jointly with spectrum and modulation format conversion in SBPP-BASED elastic optical networks
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper proposes regenerator sharing with spectrum and modulation format conversion in shared backup path protection (SBPP)-based elastic optical network (EON). We propose an efficient heuristic algorithm (RSR-SBPP) for dynamically routing and spectrum assignment and for placing and sharing regenerators in an SBPP-based EON, so as to minimize the number of regenerators and maximize protection resource sharing. This algorithm achieves lower probability of bandwidth blocking (BBP) compared to conventional Fixed Route (FR) algorithm and 1+1 protection. The BBP performance is also seen to saturate with an increasing number of regenerators.

articleTitle: Dynamic monitoring of crude oil magnetic treatment by etched Fiber Bragg Gratings
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: To design an effective Magnetic Fluid Conditioner, the etched Fiber Bragg Grating (eFBG) being demodulated by the energy system is designed to optimize magnetic density and treatment time. During oil magnetization, the peak energy increases monotonically with time elapsing till a critical value and then almost keeps a constant. During oil demagnetization, the peak energy decreases sharply and slows down subsequently after a critical value. Two turning points could quantitatively predict magnetization and demagnetization completion, respectively. After being encapsulated by suitable mechanical structure, the etched FBG system could detect dynamically the flowing crude oil under the magnetic field, which means it is feasible for coefficient optimization in MFC.

articleTitle: Efficient and stable QKD scheme based on differential phase shift and polarization coding
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose an improved scheme of hybrid quantum key distribution based on the combination of differential phase shift and BB84 polarization encoding. By adjusting the polarization properly and routing all the probability amplitudes to interfere, a higher protocol efficiency of 3/2 is obtained. A better stability can be achieved with the birefringence effects and polarization-dependent losses at the transmitter compensated automatically by employing Faraday mirrors and quantum bit error rate can be smaller by reducing single photon detectors with fewer time slots introducing dark counts. Moreover, the condition for stable interference at the receiver is provided and the security performance is demonstrated, specifically.

articleTitle: Research on metro intelligent optical network planning and optimization
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: With the rapid growth and construction of information, the traditional voice-based static network has been gradually changed to dynamic network. By analyzing the current equipment situation and transmission services of metropolitan area network, some short comings which exist in the current transmission network come to conclusion. On the basis of the state-of-art transmission equipment, an efficient and intelligent network planning method via OTN/ASON/PTN is proposed. Combined with the actual business situation, the advantages of intelligent optical network have been verified after the contrast between traditional and the intelligent optical network.

articleTitle: Dynamic traffic grooming based on auxiliary graph in spatial division multiplexing enabled elastic optical networks
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An auxiliary graph (AG) is designed to address traffic grooming under dynamic traffic scenario in spatial division multiplexing enabled elastic optical networks (SDM-EON). Various traffic grooming policies are achieved by adjusting the edge weights of AG, and evaluated through simulation in terms of spectrum efficiency and inter-core crosstalk. Numeric results show that the proposed SDM grooming reduces the effect of crosstalk by decreasing the used cores.

articleTitle: Wireless temperature monitoring system based on FBG and Zigbee
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper presents a wireless temperature monitoring system based on FBG and ZigBee, this system gets FBG sensor and wireless communication together, FBG sensor has high precision, stable performance, and wireless communication has advantage on flexible application. So the system solves wiring trouble, weak adaptability, and so much problems brings by the traditional distributed wireless temperature monitoring system. Firstly, introduces the working principle of FBG, and designed a communication system which based on NFR24L01 module and SCM. Finally, measured the system has a high quality of communication. The construct of this system is convenient, the use of it is simple. Thus, it meets a great utility value.

articleTitle: High-mode mid-infrared supercontinuum source based on low-loss fusion spliced silica and chalcogenide fiber
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A 1.8 to 4.2 μm high-mode mid-infrared supercontinuum (SC) is presented in an all-fiber chalcogenide-based system. In this experiment, 3-m-long step-index As<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> fiber with a core diameter of 9 μm is fusion spliced with a piece of ultra-high numerical aperture fiber, achieving a low splicing loss of about 0.2 dB. When a 1.9-2.5 μm nanosecond SC is adopted as the pumping source, a SC spanning from 1.8 to 4.2 μm is obtained in the piece of fusion spliced As<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> fiber with a maximal average power of 133 mW. Over 70% power is shifted to wavelengths longer than 2400 nm. The measured beam profile of the output beam demonstrated its LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> operation within the wide spectral range between 1.8 to 3.5 μm.

articleTitle: A novel approach for photonic generation of tunable linearly chirped microwave waveform with large time-bandwidth product
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We present a novel photonic approach based on heterodyne between a multiple-dispersed optical pulse and a continuous optical signal to generate tunable linearly chirped microwave waveform (LCMW) with large time-bandwidth product (TBWP). The carrier frequency of the generated waveform can be changed by tuning the frequency of continuous optical wave outputted from the tunable laser source (TLS),while the TBWP of the LCMW can be changed by optically pumping the linearly chirped fiber Bragg grating (LCFBG) in the dispersive loop with different pumping powers. An extremely large equivalent dispersion will be obtained because of the dispersive loop used in the system, which leads to the generation of LCMW with long temporal duration. The capability of the presented method is verified via numeric simulation.

articleTitle: Research on ultraviolet response enhancement technology of linear array CCD
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Compared to coating on the photosensitive surface of the thinned back-illuminated CCD, the coating on the surface of the front-illuminated (FI) CCD is relatively simple, controllable and cheaper which shows great market value. The ultraviolet (UV) response enhancement technology of the FI CCD is studied based on a spin-coating method. After the fluorescent powder is coated on the photosensitive surface of the CCD, the CCD is assembled in the micro UV spectrometer prototype. The UV responses of the CCD are compared before and after coating. The results indicate that the UV spectrum response of CCD is greatly enhanced at the range of 200~313 nm after coating. Moreover, the intensity of discrete spectrum is improved but the resolution of the spectrometer is not changed.

articleTitle: Realization of sub-wavelength imaging in the THz waveband
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Terahertz (THz) imaging has become a hot research topic because of its wide applications ranging from biomedical science to astronomy. However, its resolution is also limited by the diffraction limit. Surface plasmonic resonance is a well-known technology that can manipulate the electromagnetic wave in the sub-wavelength region. This paper proposes a method based on surface plasmonic resonance to break the diffraction limit in THz waveband, and presents the preliminary experiment results, where sub-wavelength resolution was achieved.

articleTitle: Evaluation of transmission performance of OAM-based FSO links with Laguerre-Gauss beams and Bessel-Gauss beams
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Transmission probability spectrum, signal to crosstalk ratio and channel capacity of OAM-based FSO links in Kolmogorov turbulence are investigated by using Laguerre-Gaussian (LG) beams and Bessel-Gauss ( BG) beams, respectively. The results reveal the BG beams have a smaller crosstalk probability spectrum expansion, higher signal to crosstalk ratio and the channel capacity of BG beams is also much closer to the ideal value than the LG beams in the same turbulent environment.

articleTitle: Highly sensitive fiber-optic accelerometer by using grating inscription in depressed cladding fibers
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel structure, in which a short section of depressed cladding fiber stub containing a Bragg grating is spliced to a single-mode fiber, is proposed in this work. Experimental results, through monitoring the total reflection power from the core and depressed cladding, have demonstrated that the proposed sensor is very sensitive to fiber bending and weak vibration (<;0.3 m/s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) in the low frequency range (<;10 Hz).

articleTitle: STM32F4 based real-time peak detection of FBG
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A low-cost and compact FBG demodulator is demonstrated and high efficiency peak detection method is implemented for it. A low-cost Tunable laser is used as light source, so bulky and often expensive light dispersion device is not needed. Low-cost and compact STM32F4 embedded ARM system is used to acquire data and to detect the peak. High efficiency Gaussian curve fitting method based on Levenberg-Marquardt (LM) algorithm was developed to detect the peak wavelength. The demodulation time is only 70ms. The uncertainty of the peak detection is 0.87 pm when the tuning stop is 10pm. It it is suitable for field use where real-time measurement is needed.

articleTitle: Adaptive routing and spectrum allocation in Elastic waveband switching Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Several lightpaths can be switched as a single entity, so that only one pair of transmission ports will be consumed at every intermediate node, which facilitates port savings in Wavelength-Division Multiplexing (WDM) optical networks. However, in Elastic Optical Networks (EONs), the lightpath does not occupy a fixed wavelength but a group of continuous and orthogonal subcarriers with the flexible bandwidth provisioning adjusted under the distance adaptive modulation. This means that the waveband switching in EONs involves the multi-dimensional allocation of the subcarrier, wavelength and even waveband, with the high dynamic. In this paper, to minimize the port cost and efficiently utilize spectral resources with the help of the complementary advantages of waveband switching and EONs, we propose the modulation-adaptive algorithm followed by a new waveband switching strategy. Simulation results demonstrate that our approach is cost-effective and improves the spectral efficiency of elastic waveband switching optical networks.

articleTitle: Experiment of audio visual communication system based on white LED and intelligent mobile terminal
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: With the innovation of mobile digital terminals and the development of visible light communication system, how to combine mobile terminals and existing visible light communication systems will become an important issue. This paper puts forward one kind of visible light communication system, which is used in the room with the earphone jack as the receiving channel of the mobile terminal. The system takes the commercial white light emitting diodes as the transmitter, and the receiver is composed of a high sensitivity PIN and a mobile phone. This system utilize QPSK-OFDM modulation format, and the relationship among bit error rate, transmission rate and distance is investigated. When the transmission rate is lower than 16 kB/s, bit error rate (BER) in this system are under the error threshold within 1 meter.

articleTitle: Terahertz modulator based on graphene-embedded waveguide
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We reported a novel terahertz modulator based on graphene-embedded waveguide. Comparing to previous solution, the terahertz wave-matter interaction in the modulator structure is enhanced greatly. In theory, the modulation depth can be nearly 100% as the simulation results show. Experimental characterisations are carried out through continuous terahertz wave system and the terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (TDZ) system respectively. The best experimental modulation depth is 29.53%, which is much larger than state-of-art results.

articleTitle: The cost-efficient all-optical wavelength conversion for 160 Gbps CO-OFDM signal based on SOA
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: All-optical wavelength conversion (AOWC) for 160Gbps polarization division multiplexing OFDM (PDM-OFDM) 16QAM signal in semiconductor optical amplifier (SOA) is theoretically simulated and realized in this paper. An external cavity laser is employed as the dual-pump seed. The measured result shows that the polarization insensitive converted signals can be achieved based on coherent detection without crosstalk. The simulation results verify the correctness of the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Cost-optimized line-rate and modulation-format selection in survivable flexible bandwidth optical networks
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we address the cost-optimized line-rate and modulation-format selection in survivable flexible bandwidth optical networks. Two different transponder configuration approaches are proposed to minimize network cost by employing the dedicated and shared optical transponders on working path and backup path.

articleTitle: Research on the solution refractive index sensor based on the microfiber coupler
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The periodic optical power distribution of the optical microfiber coupler is calculated by numerical simulation with beam propagation method. A kind of solution sensor using microfiber coupler (MFC) surrounded with sucrose solution is experimentally demonstrated, and the experimental results show that the sensitivity of the sensor is wavelength-dependent. Both theoretical and experimental results have shown that the solution sensor is sensitive to the surrounding refractive index. With surrounding sucrose solution refractive index ranging of 1.330-1.400RIU,the resonant wavelength shifting has good linear relationship with surrounding refractive index changes, and the response sensitivity reaches to 1901.34 nm/RIU.

articleTitle: Fabrication and sensing characteristics of chiral long-period fiber gratings written in the single-mode fiber by CO2 laser
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrated the fabrication of the chiral long-period grating (CLPG) with the helical structures by twisting conventional single-mode fibre while the fibre was exposed unilaterally by CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> laser. The bending and surrounding refractive index characteristics of the fabricated CLPG were investigated experimentally. Experimental results show that the CLPG has high bending sensitivity of 19.336 nm/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> and refractive index sensitivity of 932.86 nm/RIU.

articleTitle: The all-fiber electro-absorption modulator based on quadri-layer graphene
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An all-fiber structured electro-absorption (EA) modulator based on quadri-layer graphene is proposed. The quadri-layer graphene is directly built into the core of the fiber to ensure the coupling efficiency. Mode analysis is used to reveal the light modulation mechanism under the anisotropic graphene modeling, which is merely conducted in previous studies. Compared with conventional semiconductor EA modulators, it exhibits an excellent performance with the advantages such as small footprint (12.9 μm), high modulation depth (0.233 dB/μm), small voltage swing (0.2 V), low energy consumption and broad operation bandwidth. In addition, the proposed modulator features simple structure, low optical propagation and coupling loss, and good integrated compatibility as the fiber modulator. All these edges prospect the great potentiality in future high-speed optic fiber communications, optical signal processing, and all-fiber systems.

articleTitle: Performance investigation of the FFT/IFFT size efficient DFT-Spread-OFDM signals in hybrid Fiber-VLLC systems
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, DFT-Spread and ISFA enabled FFT/IFFT size efficient orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) is experimentally demonstrated in an intensity-modulation and direct-detection (IMDD) hybrid fiber-visible laser light communication (Fiber-VLLC) system. The experimental results show that, after 20-km standard single mode fiber (SSMF) and 5-m wireless transmission, the bit error rates (BERs) of 3.17 Gbps (4.75 Gbps) 16-QAM (64-QAM) DFT-Spread FFT/IFFT size efficient OFDM signals with less than 1e-5 (1e-2) can be achieved. In addition, the FFT/IFFT size efficient DFT-Spread OFDM with lower power consumption can obtain a similar performance compared to conventional DFT-Spread IMDD OFDM.

articleTitle: Photonic generation of phase-coded microwave signals based on a micro-ring polarization rotator
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A photonic approach for the generation of widely tunable phase-coded microwave signals based on a novel micro-ring polarization rotator (MRPR) is theoretically proposed. The MRPR is a micro-ring with asymmetric waveguides structure in the coupling region. The device has the characteristics of both polarization rotation and wavelength selection, which can make the carrier and sideband orthogonally polarized. The generation of phase-coded signals with tunable frequencies at 20 and 30GHz are simulated.

articleTitle: A fiber microfluidic velocity sensor based on polarization maintaining fiber
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a polarization maintaining fiber (PMF) is used as the sensing element for microfluidic velocity measurement. The proposed fiber microfluidic velocity sensor adopts the Sagnac loop structure, where the PMF is incorporated in the fiber loop. The microfluidic velocity measurement is realized by monitoring the output spectrum of the Sagnac loop. Different microfluidic velocity causes different pressure on the side of the PMF, which leads to the wavelength shift of the output spectrum of the Sagnac loop. Experimental results show that a quadratic relationship between the microfluidic velocity and the dip shift of the output spectrum has been observed with the microfluidic velocity range from 0~900um/min. The proposed microfluidic velocity fiber sensor owns significant behavior in various applications such as chemical engineering and medical equipment technology.

articleTitle: Secrecy capacities of optical CDMA communication systems based on gold codes
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Optical CDMA transmission systems can not only increase system capacity, but also achieve physical- layer security against fiber tapping attacks. In this paper, we examine the information-theoretic security of optical CDMA systems by evaluating the tradeoff between the achieved information capacity and the confidentiality. Moreover, we also evaluate the impacts of key system parameters, such as the number of users M, the number of stages of shift-register r (or code lengths L=2r-1) and the input optical power P, on the secrecy capacity and the interception probability. Our results indicate that key system parameters play an important role in enhancing the secrecy capacities, thus choosing suitable values of these system parameters will be helpful to improve the secure performance of optical CDMA systems to some degree.

articleTitle: Improved radio-over-fiber-based distributed antenna system with antenna diversity for passive UHF RFID
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Passive radio frequency identification (RFID) is an automatic identification technology which has been widely used in the field of the Internet of Things (IOT). In this paper, a RoF-based DAS RFID system with antenna diversity is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. The dynamic sensitivity of uplink is specially considered and photonics lantern (PL) is used to reduce the loss of signal combination. In order to verify the ability of the proposed system, we conduct a series of experiments depends on different number of tags and different transmitting power levels with the proposed system and RF switchable system in a typical lab environment. The experimental results show that the new approach improve the tag detection speed by almost 15% over a sparse environment and 10% over a dense environment respectively, compared with a RF switchable RoF DAS RFID system. The new approach is more accurate and faster than the RF switchable system with the same reader transmission power.

articleTitle: All-optical signal up-conversion based on a directly modulated DFB semiconductor laser and an optoelectronic oscillator
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An all-optical signal up-conversion scheme using a directly modulated DFB semiconductor laser and an optoelectronic oscillator is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. By directly modulating a DFB semiconductor laser, a higher modulation efficiency and a lower conversion loss are achieved comparing with the modulators based schemes. The 40 Mb/s 16QAM signal working at 1 GHz is successfully up-converted to 10.68 GHz. The conversion loss is independent of the frequency and the power of the intermediate-frequency signal.

articleTitle: Influence of input beam radius of curvature on the excited modes of an MMF for high speed applications
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Effect of input beam radius of curvature on the power coupling efficiencies of different modes excited in a multimode fiber (MMF) for high speed applications are investigated for two axial launching methods. As compared to the popular center launching (CL) method, mode field diameter matched center launching (MFDM-CL) is less affected by curved wavefronts.

articleTitle: Phase splitting timing recovery for coherent optical transmission systems
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A new feedback symbol timing recovery technique using timing estimation joint equalization is presented for digital receivers with two samples/symbol or higher sampling rate. The clock recovery algorithm in this paper is different from the traditional method, using different algorithm by distinguishing the phase of adjacent symbols. A new timing algorithm is proposed for the adjacent signals with same phase to estimate the timing offset accurately. It is also shown that by adding the part of eliminating phase modulation interference before timing estimation, the variance can be further reduced, resulting in a smoothed timing estimate. The MSE and BER of the resulting timing estimate are simulated, supporting a satisfactory estimation performance. Good clock tone performance is obtained for MQAM modulation formats and roll-off factor (ROF) values close to 0.

articleTitle: Multiple data sources fusion method for effectiveness evaluation of ship-borne TT&C system
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel method which synthesizes the expert experiences and test data to evaluate the effectiveness of space tracking, telemetry and command (TT&C) system is proposed. The data sources include qualitative indexes and quantitative indexes. Unified expression of heterogeneous data is realized by belief map as data description form. Taking optimization and reduction to the indexes system, using belief map as data description form, using extensive Bayesian algorithm to fuse data from multiple sources, the fusion evaluation framework is given. Taking effectiveness evaluation of USB TT&C system as an example, this paper demonstrates that the data fusion method has a certain practicability and validity, which can effectively improve the reliability and credibility of evaluation results.

articleTitle: Nitride-based p-i-n ultraviolet bandpass photodetectors with short-wave barrier layer
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we present a numerical simulation study of nitride-based p-i-n ultraviolet bandpass photodetectors, which was designed with a high Al composition AlGaN unipolar barrier layer. The AlGaN unipolar blocking layers act as potential barrier that reduce the collection of carriers generated by high energy photons in p-Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.1</sub>Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.9</sub>N short-wave filter layer. Compared to the conventional nitride-based p-i-n band-pass photodiodes, this new structure devices are capable high short-wave rejection ration. To validate the model, we compared the simulation predictions with experimental data of conventional p-i-n bandpass photodiodes published in the literature. This concept can be applicable for any p-i-n photodetectors.

articleTitle: Simulation study on observation of space target through atmosphere based on angular spectrum theory
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Atmosphere plays a significant role on the observation effects of space target from the ground. Theoretical model based on angular spectrum propagation is built up to simulate and investigate the influence of atmosphere on the observation. Influences from distribution of atmosphere's refractivity, turbulence, altitude angle, target's shape and observation wavelength are simulated and discussed, which will be helpful when practical observation is performed.

articleTitle: Influence of ambient temperature on the performance of the semiconductor laser
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper,the influence of ambient temperature on the performance of the semiconductor laser is systematically investigated in theory. We built the simulation model, and the simulation results indicated that Ambient temperature changes would affect the laser chip temperature, resulting in the laser vital parameters in simulation results.

articleTitle: Intensity-modulated fiber-optic refractive index and strain sensor based on miniaturized modal interferometer
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel intensity-modulated fiber-optic refractive index (RI) and strain sensor based on modal interferometer (MMI) is proposed. The sensing mechanism is mainly based on the Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) constructed by one down taper spliced between dual up tapers on the single mode fiber (SMF). High-order cladding modes are efficiently excited owing to the mismatch of the mode filed diameter (MFD). Experimental investigations achieve a RI sensitivity of -22.437dBm/RIU and a strain sensitivity of 0.0008dBm/με with R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 0.9972 and 0.9962 respectively. It has to be noted that this MMI is only made of single SMF and is of low cost and easy fabrication.

articleTitle: An optical fiber biosensor based on layer-by-layer electrostatic self-assembly for rapid detection of HIgG
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we designed an optical fiber biosensor for rapid detection of HIgG, which is simple, cost-effective and can be easily fabricated. The average detection time is about 20 minutes. A thin core optical fiber with a length of 2 cm was fused between two segments of single mode optical fibers. The outside surface of the thin core optical fiber was coated with the antibody using the method of layer-by-layer electrostatic self-assembly, and then was able to detect the antigen in solution. We selected Human Immunoglobulin G (HIgG) as the antigen in the experiment. The working performance of our biosensor with different layers of the electrostatic film was investigated. Best sensitivity was achieved to be 16.92 nm/(mg/mL) when the layers was five. Best limit of detection (LOD) of our biosensor was calculated to be 0.59mg/L. Besides, NaCl solution and bovine serum albumin (BSA) solution were also added during the experiments, which showed negligible wavelength shift compared with HIgG solutions. This confirmed the specificity of our biosensor. The proposed optical fiber biosensor has good application potential in other medical or biological fields.

articleTitle: Transmission performance evaluation of uncoupled multicore fiber based on linewidth induced crosstalk statistical distribution
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A model which can predict long-haul transmission performance of multicore fiber (MCF), with a tradeoff of accuracy and complexity, is highly desired. We analytically validate the Gaussian distribution of linewidth induced multicore fiber (MCF) crosstalk. Then, a modified Gaussian noise (GN) model including the MCF crosstalk is verified through simulations. It is found that transmission capacity using ring-structure MCF with mean crosstalk of −45 dB per 100 km can almost approach to that of N parallel single mode fibers (SMFs).

articleTitle: Design of a cascaded narrow bandpass filter based on 2-D photonic crystals
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A model of cascaded narrow bandpass filter is proposed. The structure of the filter with a resonator and two reflectors is used as the cascaded unit. The parameters of the cascaded filter are analyzed theoretically by coupled mode theory and transfer matrix method. The studies illustrate that the bandwidth of the filter with two reflectors could be controlled by adjusting the phase parameters of which. Furthermore, a flat-top and sharp roll-off response could be achieved if the filter unit is cascaded. Based on the model, a cascaded narrow bandpass filter based on 2-D photonic crystals is presented in this paper and the parameters of which are analyzed by finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method. The simulation results show that the center frequency is 193.4 THz, the insertion loss is less than 0.27dB, and the 3dB bandwidth is about 156 GHz.

articleTitle: Nonlinear transmission and phase noise tolerance of different 8-ary constellations using Viterbi-Viterbi carrier phase estimation
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The nonlinear transmission and phase noise tolerance performance of three different 8-ary constellations (8PSK, star-shaped 8QAM and circular 8QAM) in coherent optical communication systems are investigated with the improved Viterbi-Viterbi algorithms for carrier phase estimation and radius-directed linear Kalman filter for polarization de-multiplexing.

articleTitle: Detection of nonlinear frequency division multiplexed path-averaged solitons
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we study the detection of 3-eigenvalue nonlinear frequency division multiplexed (NFDM) path-averaged solitons after their propagation from one 50-km to three 50-km spans of standard single mode fiber (SSMF) with coherent detection. Based on the recently developed nonlinear Fourier transform (NFT), the eigenvalues of NFDM average solitons are calculated by using Ablowitz-Ladik algorithm. Simulation results show that the location of eigenvalues is robust to the variation of both the signal power and the fiber length to a certain extent.

articleTitle: Fiber optic pressure and temperature monitoring system for downhole application
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A Pressure and temperature (P&T) monitoring system based on fiber Bragg grating (FBG) and extrinsic Fabry-Perot interferometer (EFPI) for downhole application is designed and tested. The system is electronically passive, with no electronics downhole, and can monitor downhole pressure and temperature continuously without breaking in production of oil well. It is demonstrated in experimental well test that the system measurement error is less than 1 °C for temperature and 0.03 MPa for pressure. The system is installed in a production well and monitor the downhole P&T for a year at the temperature of 140°C and the highest pressure of 50 MPa.

articleTitle: Full-functional all-optical flip-flop based on polarized Sagnac loop
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel type of all-optical D, S-R, J-K and T flip-flop based on polarization Sagnac loop is investigated in this paper, which adopts highly nonlinear of hollow-core photonic crystal fiber (HC-PCF). The novel all-optical flip-flops (AOFFs) can decrease the length of circuit, the input power, and the transmission loss. The principles and characteristics of Sagnac loop are analyzed and the design of each type is presented. The numerical results show that, for 100 Gb/s transmission system, the input power can less than 50 μW and the switching time is in few picoseconds.

articleTitle: A new performance evaluation method of multi-sensors co-detection based on the object's geometric shape
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, the objective evaluation of the performance of multi-sensor cooperative detection is studied. A new method to evaluate the performance of multi-sensor cooperative detection is proposed based on the object's geometric shape. The method utilizes the property that extend fractal characteristic of target is sensitive to the size and contrast of the target, searching for the fractal characteristics of the target from the fractal characteristics of the target shape measure, so as to evaluate the performance of cooperative detection. This method can give an objective and quantitative evaluation result under the condition of lack of ground truth record. The simulation experiment is carried out using the actual measured data. The experimental results prove the efficacy of the method.

articleTitle: An optical pulse position modulation based on double-circle iteration
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we have proposed an optical pulse position modulation based on double-circle iteration, targeting at the next generation of high speed optical metropolitan area networks. The focuse of this paper lies on the performance of spectral efficiency, the bit error rate and chromatic dispersion. The proposed modulation format is also compared to on-off-keying(OOK) and 4-level pulse-amplitude modulation(PAM4). The results show a clear advantage of bit error rate and dispersion tolerance, thus it can achieve longer fiber delivery distance.

articleTitle: A tunable multi-passband microwave photonic filter
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this article, we have proposed and demonstrated two new approaches to implement microwave photonic filter with tunable multi-passband based on reflective fiber Mach-Zehnder interferometer and cascaded fiber Mach-Zehnder interferometers and dispersive medium. The proposed MPF has simple structure and is easy to implement, also the experimental results show good tunability and switch performances.

articleTitle: Tunable fiber laser based on cascade structure consisted of an in-line M-Z and Sagnac loop
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A tunable Erbium-doped fiber laser is proposed by cascading an in-line M-Z and Sagnac loop. Four laser output was gotten and were stable. With the combined effect of erbium-doped fiber gain spectrum and in-line M-Z structure transmission, gain maximum was at 1550nm waveband. At the same time, four laser output was gotten because of the frequency selecting effect of Sangac. When temperature increased from 30 °C to 150 °C, the center wavelength output of the first wavelength in the laser can be tuned from 1548.5nm to 1557.4nm. And the output power of the four wavelength is stable.

articleTitle: Precoding assisted direct detection optical FBMC for 100 Gbit/s short-range transmission system
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A 4×25.1 Gbit/s WDM system based on intensity modulation and direct detection is presented. 50-km SSMF transmission of 32QAM-FBMC was realized with BER under FEC limit. Moreover, a receiver sensitivity improvement of nearly 1.5 dB was achieved by introducing CAZAC-Precoding.

articleTitle: Raman frequency shift based light source at 1.66um for DTS application
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In order to improving the sensing length of the Distributed Optical Fiber Temperature Testing System (DTS), a broadband pulsed source at 1.66um was proposed and demonstrated. A Raman frequency shifter, composed of a certain length single mode fiber (SMF) and a fiber band-pass filter was used as a key device to obtain the proposed light source. By changing the output power of the pump laser, the proposed broadband light source at 1.66um can be achieved with a bandwidth of ∼30nm, a pulse peak power of 18 W, pulse duration and repetition rate are, at all the same with the pump laser, 5ns∼1000ns and 1Hz∼100kHz respectively. In addition, relationships among output power of pump laser, fiber length in frequency shifter and output power at 1.66um were discussed. These characters facilitate a longer range DTS sensing with the spatial resolution maintaining.

articleTitle: Tunable microwave photonic signal processing
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Microwave photonic technologies are attractive for processing high bandwidth signals, overcoming inherent limitations with electronic approaches. Recent new developments in tunable microwave photonic signal processing are presented in the paper, including compensation techniques to achieve high-performance processors, wideband tunable time delays and phase shifting, and programmable microwave photonic filters with arbitrary frequency response characteristics.

articleTitle: Design of Media Access Control in visible light communication system and a simple way to avoid dual transmit over dual Access Point
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Visible light communication (VLC) has won much attention in recent years. In this work, an experimental visible light communication system of its' Media Access Control (MAC) layer on the digital signal process and a simple method to avoid one packet dual transferred between two or more Access Point (AP) is presented. The work is implemented in FPGA (Field Programmable Gate Array), which are based on IEEE 802.15.7 protocol. RTC/CTS frames are used to eliminate hidden terminals. The simulation result of Throughput is above seventy percent of its' PHY rate under ten terminals. The real PHY rate is 30Mbit/s.

articleTitle: Novel bend-resistant large mode area fiber with combination structure of multi-trench and leakage channel
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A bend-resistant large mode area fiber with combination structure of multi-trench and leakage channel is proposed. In terms of the practical requirement for active fibers, the core region is designed with a higher refractive index than the pure silica, which allows the core to be highly doped with gain medium. In the meantime, a ring of high-index rods are introduced to work as the resonant ring, which also forms leakage channels for the higher order modes to leak out. Four layers of high-index trenches are introduced into the core to modulate the mode field distribution and suppress bend distortion. It achieves single mode operation at a tight bend radius of 15 cm with a mode field area of 1310 µm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Formaldehyde sensor based on zeolite thin film-coated spherical end-face fiber
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a novel zeolite thin film-coated spherical end face fiber sensor for detecting formaldehyde. The proposed sensor comprise of the fiber's spherical end-face covered with a layer of zeolite thin film. The zeolite film and spherical end face constituted an arc-shaped inline Fabry-Perot cavity, which improved the interference performance. The concentration of formaldehyde was measured by monitoring the wavelength shift and intensity change of F-P interference which induced by the formaldehyde adsorption of the zeolite film. Experimental results showed that the sensitivity was about 5 pm/ppm when the concentration ranged from 0 ppm to 6000 ppm. The sensitivity for the intensity at 1541.9 nm was 0.002 dB/ppm in the concentration range from 0 ppm to 4000 ppm. The sensitivities for the intensity at 1577.1 nm were −0.001 dB/ppm in the concentration range from 0 ppm to 3000 ppm and −0.003 dB/ppm in the concentration range from 3000 ppm to 6000 ppm. The OSA with a 0.02nm measurement precision was used in our experiments, so the precision could reach about 4 ppm in the concentration range from 0 to 6000 ppm.

articleTitle: A Software Defined Radio Access Network based on inter-cell interference suppression
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The convergence of optical and wireless network has led to the trend of future access network . Under the study of Software Defined Radio Access Network(SD-RA) and Soft Frequency Reuse(SFR) system model, this paper presents a new inter-cell interference suppression algorithm of SD-RA network. The paper also summarizes and analyses the difference between the SFR based on coordinate multi-point transmission (CoMP) and SD-RA. The computer simulation results show that the inter-cell interference suppression algorithm can bring about 5dB SINR (Signal to Interference plus Noise Ratio) gain.

articleTitle: Interleaved frequency division multiple access for uplink VLC
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose an uplink visible light communication (VLC) scheme based on interleaved frequency division multiple access (IFDMA), which provides some highly desirable features such as high spectral efficiency and high tolerance against multipath distortion. Compared with OFDMA, the IFDMA has lower PAPR and lower computation complexity at the transmitter. The experiment results show that the increased transmission span is about 7.5-cm at a BER of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−5</sup> for IFDMA compared with the OFDMA.

articleTitle: An RF photonic frontend for multi-channel broadband communication payloads
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An RF photonic frontend for multi-channel broadband communication payloads has been proposed to face high frequency satellites challenges demanding higher bandwidth and explosive data bytes. The proposed scheme features broadband, light weight, small size compared with conventional RF frontend in a pure microwave approach. Furthermore, we carry out proof-of-concept experiments and present performance results of the overall frontend, which verifies our assumptions.

articleTitle: Laser assisted welding of layered metallic nanostructure
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We present laser assisted welding of the layered metallic nanostructure, including two gold NWs and insulating layers, to reveal a prominent approach to interconnect the nanostructures in different layers. Since these nanostructures are building blocks for plasmonic integrated circuits, this work provides a promising and simple technology for the development of nanowire-related plasmonic or electric interconnect.

articleTitle: 1.63–1.73 µm tunable all-fiber femtosecond pulse generation from a P-doped Raman fiber pumped by 1.56 µm dissipative soliton
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report a 1.63–1.73 µm femtosecond pulse based on the Raman self-frequency-shift of a 960 m P-doped Raman fiber. The seed source is 1,56 µm dissipative solitons with the pulse duration of 7.5 ps and the repetition frequency of 7.71 MHz. The Raman self-frequency-shift in the P-doped Raman fiber results in the tunable wavelength only by adjusting the input power. As the input power increases, nonlinear optical effect such as self-phase modulation(SPM) and four-wave mixing(FWM) begin to take effect, which results in the broad spectrum range. Finally, we obtain the ∼100 nm wavelength tuning range and ∼970 femtosecond soliton pulses with a maximum input power of 120 mW after the second stage amplifier.

articleTitle: A novel pre-coding orthogonal full diversity space-time block coding scheme for 4×4 MIMO system
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper we consider a novel design of space-time block code combined with pre-coding module transmission system. Theory of orthogonal designs has shown that such code cannot be simultaneously orthogonal, of rate 1, with full diversity order, for more than 2 transmit antennas. We propose in this paper a new way to overcome this limitation by adding a pre-coding module before transmitting space-time block signals, this scheme is a rate 1 coding scheme with full diversity, and is also an orthogonal one thanks to the new adding pre-coding weights.

articleTitle: Novel training symbol structure for transmitter IQ mismatch compensation for PDM CO-OFDM at 100Gb/s
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a novel training symbol structure for polarization division multiplexed (PDM) coherent optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (CO-OFDM) system. We deduce the mathematical model for the scheme. Based on the given model, a novel compensation method is introduced to compensate the IQ imbalance. The theoretical analysis is validated by numerical simulation, in which we apply the Quadrature Phase Shift Keying (QPSK) modulation at a data rate of 75.211Gb/s over 50 km and data rate of 100Gb/s over 320 km transmission. Compared with the commonly used approach, the proposed scheme demonstrates better system BER performance against IQ imbalance.

articleTitle: Difference frequency detecting through beat note in RFOG system
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The Resonant Fiber Optical Gyroscope (RFOG) is an important component in the inertial navigation systems due to the small size, low cost and low power. A new method of using two semiconductor lasers locked to the clockwise resonance and the counter-clockwise resonance of a resonant is proposed. This paper analyzes the principle of beat note and do a simulation program. At last we can obtain the difference frequency through beat note between two separate semiconductor lasers, which is of significance to promote the wide application of RFOG in practical inertial systems.

articleTitle: Gas sensing with a highly birefringent microfiber photonic microcell
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report the fabrication of in-line photonic microcells (PMCs) by encapsulating tapered highly birefringent microfibers (Hi-Bi MFs) inside glass tubes. The encapsulation isolates Hi-Bi MFs from external environment and makes them more suitable for real-world applications. Gas sensing is realized by fabricating micro-channel on the PMC for ingress/egress. A fiber Sagnac loop interferometer (SLI) incorporating a Hi-Bi microfiber PMC demonstrated a gas pressure sensitivity of 599 pm/bar, and RI sensitivity of 2024 nm per refractive index unit (nm/RIU) in gaseous environment.

articleTitle: Solving the Hamiltonian path problem using optical fiber network
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: NP-Complete (Non-deterministic Polynomial Complete) problem is a famous mathematical problem, here we choose the Hamiltonian Path problem as the sample of the NP-Complete problems and put forward a method to solve it using optical fibernetwork. Instead of finding the path itself, the point of our solution is proving whether there exists such a Hamiltonian path which can travel all of the cities only once. We use optical fiberas information carriers and whether the time delay of passing through the system is equal to the sum of each node decides the existence of the Hamiltonian path. Because light has advantages of high speed of travelling and massive parallelism, utilizing this method to solve the Hamiltonian Path problem is faster than other common algorithms.

articleTitle: Liquid level sensing application based on optical chaos
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The application of liquid level sensing based on optical chaos is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. The liquid level sensor is a segment of no-core fiber (NCF) with a faraday reflection mirror (FRM) attached next to it, and with the filtering of a fiber Bragg grating (FBG), the intensity of the reflection light from the sensor is modulated by the liquid level. By monitoring the position and amplitude of the peak in the correlation curve, the measurement of liquid level and the locating of sensing point can be simultaneously achieved. Experimental result shows a linear range of 3.8 cm. This demodulation method also shows the ability of precise fault locating with the accuracy of several centimeters, making it easy for network maintenance.

articleTitle: Antimonide-based semiconductors for optoelectronic devices
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report high quality InAsSb films grown on Ge substrates with a GaAs intermediate layer via metal-organic chemical vapor deposition. The properties of the grown InAsSb films are systematically analysed. It is found that the grown InAsSb films by this method have high quality with very smooth, mirror-like morphology, and high optical quality. In particular, strong PL peak at around 3550 nm can be observed even at room temperature, which demonstrates the capabilities of the grown InAsSb films for room temperature MIR optoelectronic application. This work provides a simple and feasible strategy for the growth of high quality InAsSb films on Ge substrate.

articleTitle: Refractive index detection based on beat-frequency of cladding-carved DBR fiber lasers
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report with cladding-carved DBR fiber lasers the responses of beat frequency on external refractive index (RI). Those carves are fabricated by the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser milling technique. The device performance with different carve widths and depths are fabricated and compared with each other. The measured maximal sensitivity is up to ∼−240.4MHz/RI-unit. This study presents a useful exploration for the dual-frequency DBR fiber laser to be used in refractive index sensing and the results should be valuable for future applications of the device.

articleTitle: A novel mode-locked fiber laser based on graphene with microvoid
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this work, we demonstrate a fiber laser based on graphene which is suspended in the air. Though the damage threshold of graphene is high, it's easy to be damaged when graphene is suspended in the air. And it will form a microvoid in the middle of the graphene which acts as a saturable absorber. A stable and polarization insensitivity mode-locked fiber laser can be realized based on this graphene.

articleTitle: Direct presentation of the absorption of nanoparticles to the infrared laser and related absorption mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Upconversion NaGdF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> nanocrystals with strong upconversion luminescence were synthesized by a general solvothermal method. The size and absorption of these NaGdF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> upconversion nanoparticles (UCNPs) can be easily modulated by the doping. Furthermore, we developed a novel model by distributing NaGdF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> nanoparticles in PMMA (UCNPs@PMMA), which can be used to directly present the absorption of nanoparticles to the infrared laser and the decay process of the infrared laser, through the green fluorescence. The related absorption mechanisms were discussed.

articleTitle: Optical correlator based on single CdTe nanowire
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We have demonstrated an ultracompact optical correlator for femto-second pulse measurement based on transvers second harmonic generation (TSHG) in a subwavelength-diameter CdTe nanowire. Benefitted from the high optical nonlinearity and very small effective mode area of the nanowire, pulse energy goes down to less than 3 femtojoules per pulse.

articleTitle: Dividing orbital angular momentum of light
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: For the first time, we put forward an orbital angular momentum (OAM) divider based on coordinate transformation. The device can convert the OAM light into multiple diffracted light. The OAM of zeroth-order diffracted light is the product of the input OAM and the scaling parameter. We also extend the scheme to realize equal N-dividing of OAM. The ability of dividing OAM shows huge potential for OAM-based classical and quantum information processing.

articleTitle: High performance apodized grating coupler for 700nm Si3N4 waveguides
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: 700-nm-thick silicon nitride-on-insulator is widely used for nonlinear applications. Apodizing is extensively used in designing Si-on-insulator waveguides. Here we present a new design and optimization method for 700-nm-thick Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> grating couplers. A simulation peak coupling efficiency of -3.05 dB is achieved with the 1 dB bandwidth 51 nm. The apodized grating coupler is compatible with deep-UV lithography and only one etch step is required. The design and optimization method is instructive and meaningful for future Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> GC designing.

articleTitle: BER performance analysis of M-ary PPM over exponentiated Weibull distribution for airborne laser communications
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we use the characteristics of Meijer G function to get a closed form expression for BER of airborne optical communication systems under the combined influence of atmospheric turbulence and aero-optic effects. The atmospheric turbulence is modelled by the exponentiated Weibull (EW) distribution that can accurately describe the probability density function (PDF) of the irradiance under weak to strong condition in the presence of aperture averaging. Next, we use our derived form to study the effect of atmospheric conditions, operating wavelength and modulation level on the system performance. Moreover, the BER performance is analysed for different aperture sizes of the receiver as well. Results suggest that the aperture averaging technique can significantly improve the system performance in turbulence and aero-optics effects. Furthermore, this work is helpful for the compensate technique of system performance on airborne optical communication system.

articleTitle: Refractive index sensing characteristics of tilted long period fiber gratings
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Based on the finite difference beam propagation method (FD-BPM), we analysed the transmission spectra of tilted long period fiber gratings (TLPFGs) in detail. The new resonance dips corresponding to the LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1,m</inf> cladding modes appear at the right side of the resonance dips corresponding to the LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0,m</inf> cladding modes. While the tilted angle is equals to ∼ 86°, the coupling efficiency of new resonance dips is highest. The refractive index sensor sensitivity of new resonance dips is much higher than that of to the same order LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0,m</inf> cladding modes.

articleTitle: Research and implementation of high data rate full digital XPIC technique
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
