abstract: In the high-data transmission system, the polarization multiplexing technique is a robust way to enhance the spectrum efficiency. Due to the adverse weather and imperfections of equipments, cross-polarization interference and co-polarization attenuation have been introduced. Thus, cross-polarization interference canceller (XPIC) must be adopted to guarantee the communication QOS and reliability. In this paper, the causes and measure indexes of cross-polarization interference are analyzed; the principle of XPIC is studied. Based on the simulation of XPIC, the dual channel high data rate receiver with XPIC is developed; the experimental test system is designed. The test results show that, with the same spectral bandwidth, the transmission capability has been doubled by using the polarization multiplexing technique. Furthermore, the XPIC can be regard as a countermeasure against cross-polarization interference. When the cross-polarization discrimination is 10dB, the E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</sub>/N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> gain could reach 10dB above.

Author Keywords: dual channel high data rate receiver

articleTitle: Dispersion-tolerant upstream PON transmission scheme with improved power budget based on optical carrier suppression
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose an upstream PON transmission scheme based on optical carrier suppression at ONU and heterodyne detection at OLT. Simulation results of 25-Gb/s upstream OFDM-PON show a power budget improvement of 8-dB compared to traditional IM-DD scheme. In addition, it is observed that the scheme does not suffer from dispersion-induced power fading in traditional double sideband (DSB) transmission.

articleTitle: Optical fiber refractive index sensor based on peanut flat-end reflection structure
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An optical fiber peanut flat-end reflection refractive Index sensor based on Michelson interference principle is experimentally demonstrated. It has one peanut structure which makes it easy to fabricate and can implement measurement on the same side. The peanut structure is fabricated by electrical arc discharge. This structure constitutes a Michelson interferometer. Experimental results show that the relationship between the refractive index of the tested solution and the extinction ratio of the interference spectrum is a quadratic function, the fitting degree is 0.9915, and the refractive index measurement range is from 1.34 to 1.43. In the measurement range of refractive index from 1.34 to 1.43, its measurement sensitivity decreases with the increase of the refractive index of tested solution, when refractive index is 1.34, the maximum measurement sensitivity is 197.872 dB while the minimum measurement sensitivity is 9.394 dB when the refractive index is 1.43.

articleTitle: Dual-wavelength mode-locked thulium-doped fiber laser based on carbon nanotube
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate a dual-wavelength mode-locked thulium-doped fiber laser. The single-wall carbon nanotube is used as the mode-locker due to its large and ultrafast nonlinear optical responses. By tuning the pump power and adjusting the PC properly, stable dual-wavelength output can be achieved. The center wavelength of the dual-wavelength pulses are 1894 nm and 1907 nm, respectively. The repetition rate is about 17.64 MHz which exactly corresponds to the total length of the ring cavity. The signal-to-noise ratio is over 30 dB. It is a reliable method to realize dual-wavelength mode-locking operating at the range of 2 µm.

articleTitle: High frequency microwave phase noise measurement by photonic microwave down-conversion based on an optoelectronic oscillator
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel method for high frequency microwave phase noise measurement by photonic microwave down-conversion based on an optoelectronic oscillator is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. The measurement of single-sideband phase noise of the 10–12 GHz microwave signals under test are obtained. The phase noise floor of the measurement system is −140 dBc/Hz at 10 kHz offset.

articleTitle: High power and beam quality of a c-cut Tm,Ho:YAP laser pumped by two laser diodes
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report on a high power and beam quality of a c-cut Tm,Ho:YAP laser double-pass pumped by two 794.0-nm laser diodes. In a temperature of 77 K, an optical-optical conversion efficiency of 38.8% and a slope efficiency of 41.1% were achieved with the maximum continuous-wave (CW) output power of 14.0 W at 2044 nm. The beam quality factor M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>≈1.1 is acquired from the Tm,Ho:YAP laser by a knife-edge method.

articleTitle: Waterdrop-shaped micro-displacement sensor with high sensitivity and wide displacement variation range
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A new type of waterdrop-shaped micro-displacement sensor is proposed with high sensitivity and wide displacement variation range. A piece of commercial single mode fiber is bent into waterdrop shape with two ends of the fiber firstly passed through two metal micro tubes adhered side by side to one microstage, and then both adhered to another microstage. Interference was created at the output port of the sensor due to fiber-bending-induced birefringence. As a result, high displacement sensitivity of 556 nm/mm over a large displacement variation range of 2.08 mm is achieved by use of this type of sensor. The system is very simple and low cost.

articleTitle: A low latency and reliable peer-to-peer communication scheme with protection capability for TWDM access networks
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a dual-function scheme which supports both failure protection of the fiber links and P2P communication between RSOA-based colorless ONUs. Equivalent experiments are performed to evaluate the feasibility of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Er3+-doped fiber laser mode-locked based on single-wall carbon nanotubes
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The bidirectional operation of a single-wall carbon nanotube-based passively mode-locked erbium-doped fiber laser, is demonstrated. Differing from the conventional fiber laser, there is no isolator in the fiber laser. The laser can generate two stable pulse trains in opposite directions with different central wavelength, pulse width, and repetition rate.

articleTitle: 16-channel mode division (de)multiplexer based on densely packed bent waveguide arrays
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An ultra-broadband 16-channel mode division (de)multiplexer (MDM) based on densely packed bent waveguide arrays (DPBWAs) is experimentally demonstrated. The scheme is realized by using bent waveguides with different radius. The fabricated device, which consists of a multiplexer, DPBWAs, and a demultiplexer, exhibits insertion losses that are <; 1 dB and crosstalk that is <; -20 dB over an ~ 80 nm wavelength band.

articleTitle: Optical RF self-interference cancellation for full-duplex communication using phase modulation and sideband filtering
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel optical approach to implement the RF self-interference cancelation for full-duplex communication using phase modulation and sideband filtering is proposed and demonstrated experimentally. By using the inherent out of phase property between the left and right sidebands of phase-modulated signal, and tuning the delay time and amplitude in optical domain to align the reference signal with the interference signal, the RF self-interference cancellation is achieved. The experimental results show that, for both 5GHz and 8GHz, the system can achieve 61- and 35-dB cancellation depth for single frequency and 1MHz bandwidth, respectively.

articleTitle: Wavelength-shift-free regenerator for 10Gb/s RZ system on satellite using cascading SOAs with two-stage offset filter
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Aiming at the signal injury caused by multi-retransmission and the characteristic of dynamic routing in satellite optical network, a wavelength-shift-free regenerative scheme based on two-stage offset filter is put forward. Making use of the property that SOA with shorter or longer carrier recovery time than pulse width can lead to different spectral shift, the scheme imposes the opposite offset filter on signals respectively after two cascading SOAs, which not only gives an enhanced regenerative performance, but also keeps the wavelength unchanging before and after regeneration. The results show that the amplitude noise and power jitter can be suppressed effectively, and the Q factor of signals can be improved 8dB at most.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of high-speed spatial light modulation enabling 25-Gbit/s twisted light encoding/decoding and 260-m security free-space data transmission
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: By exploiting temporal-to-spatial domain mapping, we report high-speed spatial light modulation based on conventional spatial light modulators with slow response time. We demonstrate 25-Gbit/s twisted light (orbital angular momentum) encoding/decoding and 260-m security free-space data transmission in the experiment.

articleTitle: Low-cost optical frequency comb generator based on injected directly modulated distributed feedback semiconductor laser
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a low-cost optical frequency comb generator based on injected directly modulated distributed feedback semiconductor laser. The comb lines can be tuned by changing injection ratio, detuning frequency and polarization state of the injected signal. The experimentally generated 10 spectral lines have a flatness of 1.5 dB. To generate more spectral lines, three approaches are investigated. By adding phase modulator, 14 spectral lines within 1.8 dB power variation can be achieved.

articleTitle: B2CA: A broadcast Channel Assignment Mechanism based on branch and bound method for MRMC wireless Mesh networks
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper proposed a new broadcast Channel Assignment Mechanism for multi-radio multi-channel wireless Mesh network (WMN). The new mechanism not only use the branch and bound method to reduces the broadcast transmission redundancy, but also to avoids the potential channel interferences produced by unnecessary relay nodes and the frequency-selective-fading. The Simulation results verify the superiority of the new mechanism.

articleTitle: A Er-doped fiber laser based on feedback of random phase-shifted fiber Bragg grating
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A random fiber laser based on random phase-shifted fiber Bragg gratings, which were fabricated in a common single-mode fiber with 10 random phase-shifted points distributed, has been proposed and experimentally realized in this work. A period of 2 m Er-doped fiber provides gain amplification. It was found that the output power has linear dependence on pump power and the threshold was low about 25.2 mw. We obtained stable random lasing emission, which peak wavelength was 1551.84 nm.

articleTitle: Research on evaluation of BER in communication system
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: According to the method of BER measurement which is measured in close loop and very time consuming when the bit rate is low, the method of BER evaluation using EVM is proposed, which is using empirical equation based on equipment under test and different from traditional theoretic prediction. Experiment was carried out based on a baseband system, the difference between the predicted and the measured is smaller than 13.6%. The results show that using empirical equation to estimate the performance of object system is useful in Additive White Gaussian Noise environment. What's more, EVM reflects the effects in process directly and can be traced to the national standard.

articleTitle: Dynamic time-varying spectrum allocation algorithm in Flexible Grid Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a spectrum allocation algorithm for time-varying traffic in Flexible Grid Optical Networks considering the correlations among traffic variations. The algorithm achieves lower blocking probability and minimize number of disruptions to the live connections.

articleTitle: Electrical thermo-optic tuning of integrated polymethyl methacrylate sphere whispering gallery mode resonator
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Tuning of an integrated polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) sphere whispering gallery mode (WGM) resonator is demonstrated. The WGM resonator is constructed by inserting a PMMA sphere into an etched microstructured fiber with suspended core, where the sphere with diameter of 31.5μm functions as WGM cavity and suspended core with diameter of 1.5μm is used to feed and pick up WGMs. Experimental results show that the maximum quality factor of the proposed WGM resonator is 5.9×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> and the resonant wavelength shifts toward longer wavelength as the temperature decreases. A tuning range of 1.93nm is realized by 210mA DC current due to the thermo-optic effect.

articleTitle: High resolution static strain measurement using distributed feedback fiber laser and beat frequency technique
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A high resolution static strain measurement system using distributed feedback fibre lasers (DFB-FLs) and beat frequency technique is demonstrated. Two independent fibre lasers are used in the sensor head. One fibre laser is used to sense the strain and the other is stress-free and used as a reference. In the interrogation system, a third fibre laser is used to generate the beat notes with the two fibre lasers in the sensor head. The beat frequency difference of the two fibre laser is detected and the strain can be calculated. The experiment result shows that the static strain resolution is better than 0.25 nano-strain (nε).

articleTitle: Widely tunable ultrashort soliton source with enhanced SSFS
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A tunable ultrashort soliton source is designed by cascading a thulium-doped Fiber (TDF) to the rear of a large mode area (LMA) fiber and the shift of wavelength per power is 6.4nm/mW from 2000nm to 2200nm. The usage of TDF introduces an extra soliton self-frequency shift (SSFS) about 150nm at each pump power level. By filtering the residual pump of 1550nm, it is demonstrated that the presence of residual pump pulse further propels the soliton to longer wavelength and the absorption of TDF does not play a part in SSFS. Other factors including the increase of Raman effect, birefringence in polarization maintaining fiber are relevant but not significant.

articleTitle: Highly sensitive and specific detection of urinary Aquaporin-2 using tilted fiber grating sensors with Plasmonic nanocoatings
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Tilted fiber Bragg gratings (TFBGs), which eliminate the cross-sensitivity between environmental temperature and fiber deformation, can be designed as highly sensitive biosensors for bio-sample measurements. The miniaturized size together with the capability of remote operation makes the TFBG biosensors work in hard-to-reach places, even possible in vivo. In this work, a Plasmonic biosensor based on a TFBG coated by a 50-nm gold film for specific urinary protein (Aquaporin-2, AQP2) detection is reported. Since the biosensor is designed as a reflective probe with a length of only 10 - 20 mm (through coating a gold film as a reflection mirror in the cleaved end downstream of the grating), it is easy to insert into the media for in situ bio-sample measurement. Using this device, AQP2 concentrations in rat urine has been clearly discriminated between healthy samples and nephrotic syndrome samples, by monitoring spectral drift or intensity variation. Experimental results show that the urinary protein AQP2 can be unambiguously measured within only 15 minutes, with an intensity change of 0.3 dB.

articleTitle: Surface plasmon polariton based switch in rotary disk resonators
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We present a plasmonic switch which is composed of two Metal-Insulator-Metal (MIM) waveguides and a resonator with two symmetric half-disks. Two-dimensional (2D) finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method is used to calculate the contour profiles of field H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> and the transmission spectra of the structure. The results show that the structure can be used as an optical switch when the disk rotated, and the structure has the potential applications in future optical circuits.

articleTitle: Experimental study of wavelength switchable ER-doped fiber laser based on polarization controlling
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The wavelength switchable Er-doped fiber laser based on nonlinear polarization rotation was studied. Wavelength tuning was realized based on polarization controlling, and stable dual-wavelength operation and wavelength switchable was achieved. The central output wavelength was between 1560nm and 1593nm, and the wavelength spacing is about 10–16.5nm with a side-band suppression ration beyond 45dB, and the wavelength deviation is less than 0.05nm.

articleTitle: Temperature sensor based on curable polymer infiltrated photonic crystal fiber
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The realization and characterization of an all-solid photonic bandgap fiber (AS-PBF) with a compact size of about 10 mm by means of fully infiltrating an ultraviolet (UV) curable polymer with a high refractive index of 1.515 into air holes of a photonic crystal fiber (PCF) is demonstrated. It appears to a high wavelength sensitivity of up to -4.034 nm/°C. Compared with conventional fluid filled PBFs, the proposed AS-PBF can be stable to temperature and other environmental effects and maintain a large extinction ratio of more than 30 dB within a broad wavelength. Moreover, the splicing between the AS-PBF and single mode fibers has been solved.

articleTitle: PAPR reduction technology based on CSO algorithm in CO-OFDM system
publicationTitle: 2016 15th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a new method to reduce peak to average power ratio (PAPR) in CO-OFDM system by applying chicken swarm optimization (CSO) algorithm to optimize the initial phase of the subcarriers. Stimulation result shows that PAPR of CSO optimized signal is reduced by 5.5dB and 1.5dB compared with that of original signal and particle swarm optimization (PSO) optimized signal and BER performance is improved.
